panel: As a Devil, the AIDS Devil possesses all of the standard Devil abilities.

The AIDS Devil's personality is currently unknown.
At some point, prior to the events of Chainsaw Man, the AIDS Devil was eaten by Pochita, thus ridding its existence along with the existence of AIDS from the world.(Chapter 84)
AIDS phobia is a variant of Nosophobia and Venereophobia, respectively, the fear of developing a disease and the fear of contracting a sexually transmitted infection.
As an illness, The AIDS Devil fits within the body-related devils alongside the Blood Devil, the Ear Devil, the Legs Devil, the Mouth Devil, the Muscle Devil, the Skin Devil and the Teeth Devil.
As such, the STD Devil and the Sickness Devil can also be associated with this theme, as they embody illnesses that affect the human body.

As the embodiment of one of the era's most feared diseases, the disappearance of the AIDS Devil would have drastically diminished a major source of public fear surrounding sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections, further supporting the idea that the STD Devil has weakened significantly.
Furthermore, the erasure of the AIDS Devil likely carried particularly profound consequences given the historical context of the story, which is set in the 1990s.
It is plausible that the erasure of the AIDS Devil from existence by the Chainsaw Devil had far-reaching consequences beyond its own disappearance.

Since AIDS is a sexually transmitted disease, removing the AIDS Devil may have reduced humanity’s overall fear of sexually transmitted diseases, causing the STD Devil, who embodies the collective fear of all sexually transmitted diseases, to weaken significantly.
The AIDS Devil derives its power from AIDS phobia, the fear of developing an acquired immunodeficiency syndrome.
The status of HIV itself is presumably unchanged; however, because AIDS no longer exists, HIV infection can no longer result in the syndrome it once caused, leaving its long-term effects unknown.

This decade was defined by the global HIV/AIDS pandemic and the health scandal of contaminated blood products affecting hemophiliacs, during which numerous infections, including sexually transmitted diseases and viruses such as HIV and Hepatitis C, were spread through blood transfusions, with repercussions lasting into the early 2000s.

As a Devil, the Accident Devil possesses all of the standard devil abilities.
Besides those, not much is known about the Accident Devil's abilities.
Its body is composed of sharp, uneven surfaces resembling the aftermath of violent crashes.
Notably, a grotesque humanoid face with long hair is embedded near the lower portion of its form, evoking the imagery of victims trapped within wreckage.
The Accident Devil appears as an amalgamation of twisted cars, jagged metal fragments, and mechanical wreckage, forming a chaotic and industrial mass.
The Accident Devil's personality is currently unknown.
Yoru summons the Accident Devil and transforms it into a "Chainsaw Whip".
Yoru wields the whip to strike and overwhelm Pochita during their battle.(Chapter 216)
Additionally, after being turned into a weapon by Yoru, the Accident Devil takes the form of a whip made from tires, further emphasizing its association with vehicles.(Chapter 220)

The Accident Devil bears notable similarities to the Car Devil, as Makima states that the latter derives much of its strength from the fear of traffic accidents and being struck by vehicles.(Chapter 6)
The Accident Devil derives its power from a persistent and unjustified fear of accidents is known as Dystychiphobia, an excessive fear of all forms of physical accidents.
The Japanese name, "Jiko" (事故), directly translates to "accident," most commonly used to refer to traffic collisions in modern Japanese.
The connection is further reinforced by the Accident Devil's appearance, which is partially composed of wrecked cars, directly linking it to the concept of automobile accidents.
From there, the Aging Devil can sacrifice any organ from the agents to continuously cleave Pochita to shreds.(Chapter 186)

Fumiko Mifune states that the Aging Devil, due to having no attachment to life, is ready to make another contract with the Japanese Public Security and Government: in exchange for killing 10,000 children with Japanese citizenships, between the ages of infancy and nine, in front of mirrors, the Aging Devil will let itself be devoured by the Chainsaw Devil without putting up any resistance, removing "Aging" as a concept from the world.
It is possible, however, that its number of contracts is much higher, as it tends to transport people who do not wish to age into the Aging's World as part of a contract.

It later reveals that it wants humans to live longer so they may reach the culmination of thought on questions beyond how to escape Aging's World, and discover new concepts and unseen possibilities, even if it comes at a cost such as its death and consumption.(Chapter 185)

Naturally, it possesses all of the standard Devil abilities such as blood consumption, contract creation, etc. They appear to have made a contract with three Public Safety agents: by cutting off a finger each and writing the word "HIT" on the mirrors in blood, preceded by the names of body parts (cervical spine, neck and vertebrae, probably additional body parts to be sacrificed), the Aging Devil would proceed to strike its enemy with a single, powerful attack.

The Aging Devil is described as a transcendent being — one of the "Primal Fear" Devils that have never experienced death due to being so powerful; embodying such a concept, it can be assumed that the Aging Devil is almost as old as humanity itself.

The Aging Devil later utilizes another contract with several other Public Safety agents, one that involves using their bodies as weapons in exchange for being spared from the Chainsaw Devil's attacks.
The Aging Devil made a contract with Yoshida, Denji and Asa Mitaka, in exchange to never fight each other again, and for Yoshida, Denji, Asa, Yoru and the Aging Devil's victim to leave Aging's World.

The true extent of their power is still unknown, but they are powerful enough to overwhelm the Chainsaw Devil with a single, powerful punch and easily stop a bullet from one of Yoru's most powerful weapons (capable of even overpowering the Chainsaw Devil himself).
According to the Aging Devil, this mechanism isn't a result of its powers and is innate to humans.(Chapter 185)

After Denji vomited the head of the Snow Devil, the forest became filled with snow, implying that the alternate realm typically snows and its prior setting was due to Pochita consuming the Snow Devil.(Chapter 182)
Aging's World 老いの世界 Oi no Sekai: The Aging Devil has the ability to transport individuals to an alternate realm, which appears as a lush forest with a lake.

As shown where after being forcibly dragged into it via Pochita/Denji's stomach, the Aging Devil was also unable to access their powers when their actual body was brought there and was thus unable to kill Asa, Denji, Yoshida and its latest victim.(Chapter 190)
Hell Connection: The Aging Devil can freely manifest floating mirrors that connect directly to Hell.
However, as displayed, this manifestation is not their true body, as even the Aging Devil loses access to their powers should their true body be forcibly transported to their world.
Immense Healing Factor: While getting sliced repeatedly by Pochita with his chainsaws, it is shown to heal instantaneously.(Chapter 187)
In this reality, its residents have no need for food or water and are even incapable of dying, slowly going insane.
Like with the Darkness and Falling Devils, humanity has no means of attack that could kill a Primal Fear.(Chapter 125)
Nigh-Absolute Immortality: Devils of Primal Fear status are considered unkillable due to their power, hence why they never undergo reincarnation.(Chapter 64)
Only once the tree rots into soil, and their body and mind have become one with nature, will they be allowed to return to their original body in the real world.(Chapter 181)

Rapid-Onset Aging: The Aging Devil can make someone or something rapidly age via physical contact, to the point that it can crumble into dust in mere seconds or transform them into a tree.(Chapter 179)(Chapter 187)
Remote Harm: By sacrificing a human's body parts, the Aging Devil can cause a target to take extreme damage regardless of distance, even managing to dismember Chainsaw Man with a single strike.
The Aging Devil can manifest itself within this world, emerging their head from the trees to speak with the people that have been imprisoned there.(Chapter 184)
The Aging Devil seems to find this ability an "ugly method".(Chapter 186)

The Aging Devil's most recent victim (who made a contract with him and was transported to the Aging's World 82 years earlier) says that it is nearly impossible to escape from this reality, with only one person supposedly having succeeded.(Chapter 180)
The Devils' powers also seem to be nullified, as Yoru was unable to kill Denji, who instead reverted to human form.
The Primal Fear typically selects people who do not wish to age, bringing them to this reality as part of a contract, but can also do so forcibly, as in the case of Yoru and Denji.
These people, although on the outside look like trees, are still flesh and blood internally which can be consumed by a Devil to regenerate.(Chapter 185)
This ability also works in reverse, with humans being able to contact the Aging Devil through mirrors.
This allows it to send powerful attacks on opponents via large hands similar to that of the Hell Devil.

Time Manipulation: The Aging Devil possesses the ability to seemingly stop time, as it was able to easily stop a speeding bullet that was launched for continental travel at incredible speeds from Yoru's powerful Gun Goddess weapon, allowing them to observe and comment on it and a time-frozen Yoru before destroying the bullet and sending Yoru to the Aging's World.(Chapter 179)(Chapter 180)
Unlike a normal contract's sacrifice, where the sacrifice simply vanishes, when this ability is used the sacrifice is violently and painfully destroyed.
When reaching the culmination of thought upon arriving at some sort of answer, those who remain trapped for 1,000 or 2,000 years turn into a tree.

It sits on a throne made of flesh and bones, with human fingers decorating the back and tongues, mouths and teeth protruding from the base which is supported by the backs of two naked men with their hands cut off.
Its face, which emerges from the split head of an old person with long hair, is a smooth surface with only a mouth, connected by several strings to the two halves of the previous face.
The Aging Devil is a tall devil with a thin and gaunt physique, resembling a withered aggregate of flesh with several holes in it.
The Aging Devil's feet have raised heels, similar to stiletto shoes.
The largest hole is placed right in the center of its chest, where the heart should be.
Despite this, the Aging Devil says it wishes for humans to live longer so that their minds can reach new culmination of thoughts discover new concepts and possiblities.
However, it is shown to possess an amicable relationship with Public Safety, evident by it complimenting Yoshida for subduing Pochita.

Yoru follows up by attempting to gun down the Primal Fear with the Right Gun Gauntlet.
As such, Public Safety's plan is likely meant to eliminate the negative effects of growing old, like bone decay or mental degradation.
However, "老いる" means "growing old" hence why the name was likely selected when localizing it.

Humans naturally turning into trees after thousands of years could be seen as an alternative to dying, representing a "conclusion to life" other than death, as stated by Makima, four of which were erased by the Chainsaw Devil.
Note the lack of hands indicating a lack of "choice" in their role of carrying the elderly.
People who gaze into an ungaikyō might see a transformed, monstrous version of themselves looking back.
Some authors refer to it as gerontophobia, although this may also refer to the fear of the elderly.
Staying “forever young” is also often used as an allegory for suicide.
The Aging Devil derives its power from gerascophobia (from Greek γηράσκω: "I grow old"), an excessive anxiety about being faced with one's body changing as time passes.
The Aging Devil fits within the time-related devils alongside the Future Devil and the Eternity Devil.
The Aging Devil's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: The Aging Devil ranked 76th in the Third Popularity Poll with 299 votes.
The Aging Devil's use of mirrors could be a reference to Ungaikyō, a haunted mirror which shows demons and monsters reflected in its surface.
The name "Aging Devil" isn't entirely accurate, as "老い" specifically refers to old age, as well as referring to the elderly (though in rare instances).
The spirit which haunts this mirror, as well as the countless spirits which have been reflected in it over the years, can manipulate the reflection and cause it to appear as anything they like.

The throne it sits on, which is supported by the backs of two naked men with their hands cut off could be a reference to how in Japanese culture where it is expected from the youth to house their elderly parents when they're adults.

The way in which those who remain trapped for more than 1000 years in the Aging's World are transformed into trees recalls the punishment that Dante assigns to suicides in Canto XIII of the Inferno, transformed by contrapasso into trees or various types of plants.
The way the Aging Devil selects the victims to trap in its world follows exactly this process.
This fear is closely linked to mirrors, as those who suffer from it avoid looking at themselves in the mirror for fear of seeing that they have grown or developed wrinkles or grey hairs.
This may also be a reference to a common theme in myths where the punishment of immortality is gradual decay into nothingness, as seen in stories such as Eos and Tithonus.

Aging Devil Contract: The Aging Devil's Victim made a contract with the Aging Devil because he wanted to stop aging.
As soon as he said these words in front of a mirror, he was transported to Aging's World.(Chapter 180)
As a Devil Hunter who was good at his job, the Aging Devil Victim likely had a high level of athleticism and skill in his Devil-hunting work.
When aiding Denji's group in battling the Aging Devil, his competence is shown when he dragged the Primal Fear through Pochita's mouth by himself to trap them within its realm.
During his stay in the Aging Devil’s realm he donned a traditional fundoshi, but adapted to modern clothing after he left.
He also sports a large mole on his left cheek, in addition to noticeable eyebags, as well as laugh lines that are only visible upon close inspection.
His eyebrows are equally thick and his eyes naturally droop downward.
The Aging Devil Victim is a young-to-middle-aged Japanese man with short black hair and short but thick sideburns.
After being trapped in the Aging Devil's realm for 82 years, with no one else around his age to accompany him, he slowly began to lose his mind.
As the years went by, however, his faith in the Aging Devil dwindled, with the final straw being the introduction of Denji into their realm.

Despite this, he's shown to still be relatively lucid compared to the other victims of the Aging Devil, as his 82 years of imprisonment is rather paltry compared to the full 1000 years required for an Aging Devil victim to truly lose their sanity.
He assists Asa and Denji by informing them of how the realm works, as well as their limitations and the inevitable fate that all of the Aging Devil's victims eventually face.
He tends to have episodes of mania or insanity where he grips onto any nearby tree and wails, which Yoru reckons is his way of escaping the reality of his current situation.
He's also gone out of his way to attempt suicide on multiple occasions as a means of escape, though these attempts proved fruitless.
However, he held a deep insecurity about his physical appearance, as he was willing to make a contract with a theoretical Aging Devil just to reverse his signs of aging.
Initially, he was fine with this, as he believed that the Aging Devil chose him and a few others for a special purpose.
Prior to entering the Aging Devil's world, he's described as being the perfect Devil Hunter; proud, proficient at his job, sociable and well-respected among his peers.

The Aging Devil Victim is also shown to hold a strong moral backbone, as he vehemently protests to Denji carving open the tree-transformed victims, as he believes that due to their long imprisonment they don't deserve more suffering.
When Asa was the first person to join him in years, he wrote her off as a hallucination of a former friend that was there to keep him company.

After Asa flees and returns to him, he explains how the tree-people he encountered are the victims of the Aging Devil who remained in the realm for 1000 years, with their inevitable fate being to rot into soil which will return them to their bodies in the real world.(Chapter 181)
Denji remarks that they're probably thankful that he's doing this, to which the Aging Devil Victim remarks that the young man is a true Devil.(Chapter 187)

Feeling bitter contempt towards the Aging Devil for not only his imprisonment, but also for trapping Denji in with him, he manages to bring the Aging Devil into their own realm, allowing Yoshida to negotiate for their group's freedom.
He explains how those trapped in the Aging Devil's realm never tire or get hungry, and any attempt at suicide won't work.
He later watches Denji, Asa, and Yoshida's attempts to break out of the Aging Devil's Realm with utter shock and disbelief.(Chapter 188)(Chapter 189)
He warns Asa that travelling further into the realm will have her encounter the older inhabitants, though they're far more insane than himself.
He welcomes her to the world, before explaining that he was once a Devil Hunter that accidentally made a contract with the Aging Devil with an offhanded comment in front of a mirror.
He's later shown attempting to adjust to modern society by working as a construction worker.(Chapter 190)
He's shown to have another manic episode as Denji begins to undergo his plan of escape.(Chapter 184)
The Aging Devil victim is first shown shortly after Asa enters the Aging Devil's realm for the first time.
The man eventually snaps out of it as Denji uses his Bitterness Axe to chop at one of the human trees, protesting that the trees are fellow human beings.(Chapter 185)

Upon being asked if there truly is no way out, he remarks he heard that one person escaped beforehand, but before he can elaborate he tells her he feels as if he's about to have another manic episode again, before asking her if she's just a hallucination he thought up.(Chapter 180)
When Asa asks him where the exit is, he tells her that in his 82 years of being in the realm he hasn't found one.
When the young man attempts to do it again, he tells him that these people have lived for thousands of years and he doesn't deserve to cut them down.

Aging's World is a realm that appears as a lush forest with a lake, where time ceases to exist for the humans trapped there.
Because of that, it's possible this world is in its own separate dimension instead of a realm in the real world.
Devil Powers don't function in this world, as seen when Yoru tried to use her powers to escape but was unable to do so.(Chapter 181)
The people trapped there lose their sense of thirst, hunger and are unable to die, while slowly going insane.
These "Tree-People" are essentially victims of the Aging Devil, their bodies slowly rotting and returning to the soil, until eventually merging with nature.(Chapter 181)
Those who stay for extended periods of time, like 1,000 or 2,000 years, transform into trees.(Chapter 180)
When this process happens the trapped humans can return to their bodies in the real World.
Plot / Academy Saga / Aging Devil arc
During the fight between Pochita and Yoru both her and Asa Mitaka are sent to the Aging Devil's World, along with Yoshida and Denji.(Chapter 180)
Plot / Academy Saga / Aging Devil arc

The Devil Hunters, including Denji, Asa and Yoru, face a powerful enemy sent by Public Safety, who can manipulate the concept of aging and is willing to sacrifice itself to be consumed by Chainsaw Man,(Chapter 184) hoping to trigger a new stage of human evolution, for humanity to have a standing chance against The Prophecy of Nostradamus, by removing the concept of aging.(Chapter 186)
Plot / Academy Saga / Aging Devil arc
Ultimately, they manage to trap the Aging Devil within its own realm, then they negotiate its return to Hell and escape successfully, while leaving Tadashi Hasegawa behind.(Chapter 190)
According to the Aging Devil's Victim, there was someone who supposedly managed to escape this realm a long time ago.

The process of being sent to Aging's World could be a form of Contrapasso, a punishment that mirrors the sin of desiring immortality by preventing aging altogether, or a reference to a common theme in myths where the punishment of immortality is gradual decay into nothingness, as seen in stories such as Eos and Tithonus.

Aki also was capable of being afraid to lose those he deeply cared about.
Aki generally appeared to be a very stoic man who acted mature and sometimes blunt to the point of rudeness when he was with his fellow Devil Hunters, but he was actually fairly softhearted.
Aki was also ruthless, stating that he always makes sure the Devils he kills suffer in order to give them a slow and painful death.

Aside from Denji and Power, his change of heart regarding his outlook on Devils was best shown with the Angel Devil; he initially threatened to report him for being useless and have him be executed, but would eventually not only give up two months of his lifespan to save Angel's life, but also wrote a letter of recommendation to Public Safety for Angel to be kept alive after he lost his arms.
At first, Aki was seen to despise all Devils equally, not caring if they are Hybrids, Fiends or if they are evil by nature.

Despite being merciless, Aki still had some kindness with his fellow devil hunters, such as retrieving Denji's severed arm, taking Meowy to get medical attention, freeing Power and intentionally lying in his report to Makima in order to uncover the truth of the incident with the Bat Devil.
Despite this, he was very determined and his primary motivation for killing the Gun Devil was revenge for his family.

He could become intimidating with those he still didn't trust enough, like when he threatened Denji by telling him that if he either betrays them or sides with other Devils, he would kill him without any hesitation.

He didn't like people who don’t take their job as Devil Hunters seriously or fight for a superficial and materialistic goal like money or, in Denji's case, to be able to touch some boobs, this being one the primary reasons he and Denji didn't get along initially.
He had a tendency to get attached to others easily, and hated to see people get hurt, especially his close friends.

He told Kishibe that the reason why he wanted to leave the mission to kill the Gun Devil was because the future shown to him by the Future Devil with Denji and Power suffering a painful and terrible death, and he was scared of that future.

His air of cold detachment was a façade as he had been seen to cry over the deaths of his comrades such as Himeno and he grew to care for Denji and Power enough to try and forfeit his revenge goal in order to keep them safe.
However, he was entirely willing to put his own life on the line to save other people, even if it got in the way of his goals.
However, over the course of the story Aki slowly began to bond with some of his Devil partners to the point of genuinely caring for them and wanting to help keep them alive.
To him all Devils are the same, seeing them as nothing more than tools that can be replaced at any time.
Unlike many of his associates, he was described by Himeno as being a "normal person", in the sense that he still grieved for those lost and had not become jaded enough to close his feelings off.
After being partnered up, the two started out on a rough patch with both of them being unable to get along with each other.

Despite this, they began to warm up to each other, even to the point where they cared about each other's well-being, shown when Aki was willing to hold the Angel Devil's hand in order to save him, despite knowing that in doing so, his lifespan would be shortened.
Following the encounter with the Darkness Devil, Aki worried for the Angel Devil's life, suggesting him to form contracts with Devil Hunters in order to avoid extermination.
Furthermore, the Angel Devil was inclined to inform Aki of untold information such as the life cycle of Devils.
Much like Himeno, he also told Aki to quit the division and get another job before he gets killed.
The Angel Devil also asked Aki what he sees in Makima since it's shown he liked her, and Aki doesn't know the answer.
After fighting alongside each other and living in the same household, Aki began to consider Denji a close friend, although he still found him obnoxious at times.

Aki and Denji initially hated one another with their first mission ending up in a physical and verbal altercation, wherein Aki insults and punches Denji, only for Denji to knee him in the crotch and kick him while he's down.
Also at Makima's request, Aki allowed Denji to move into his home and took care of him.
Despite the fight, they continued to work together due to Makima's request.
He even went so far as to request the Fourth Division be exempt from fighting the Gun Devil in an attempt to keep Denji and Power safe.
He thinks Denji is a simpleton, brutish, vulgar and too unthinking to continue in a dangerous line of work.
When Aki was fighting Denji as the Gun Fiend, he imagined it as a snowball fight between friends, or possibly even brothers, as it paralleled his snowball fight with his brother in the past.
After his death, he left half of his passbook to Himeno's family.

Aki said that he usually went out to drink with many officers and even knew about their private lives, which proves he was on good terms with them.

Asa's given name, Asa アサ has the same pronunciation as the Japanese kanji for "morning" 朝 Asa, which could be interpreted as a counterpart to Yoru ヨル whose name is pronounced identically as the Japanese kanji for "night" 夜 Yoru.
Asa's surname Mitaka means "three" (三) (mi) and "hawk/falcon" (鷹) (taka).
After Pochita erases himself out of existence, thereby causing a new timeline to be created.
After being saved by Chainsaw Man, she realizes she's glad she's not dead and is no longer as negative towards other humans or towards all Devils.
Asa can be extremely socially inept, so much so that Yoru, the War Devil, shows more social awareness than her despite having limited knowledge about humanity.
Asa could relate to a family member dying because of her and tried to get him to fight "her".
Asa doesn't cope well with failure or when things don't go her way.
Asa is a quiet and unsociable girl, who dislikes her classmates, frequently wishing they would drop dead and spurning any offers of friendship.(Chapter 98)
Asa is fairly altruistic, putting herself in harm's way to save others even when she is afraid.
Asa later admits to herself that her mean-spirited attitude towards her peers was a result of jealousy and a lack of belonging.
Asa would be willing to endure bad situations if only she were to suffer, but refuses to drag others with her.

Asa's chronic tripping is a manifestation of profound subconscious self-sabotage and guilt, serving as her mind's defense mechanism against severe childhood trauma, her constant falling is later revealed to be directly tied to the deaths of her parents and a deep-seated fear of success and intimacy.
Because her brain integrated "clumsiness" as a core identity trait to hide her malicious intent, she developed a literal somatic trauma response.
Because of past experiences, she is extremely afraid of making mistakes.
Despite being capable of compassion, Asa's selfishness proves to be a hindrance even when she wants to do good.

Despite being previously shown to be very timid and frightful during Devil encounters, motivated by her desire to "save" Chainsaw Man, Asa quickly becomes a proficient Devil Hunter, seemingly having managed to become braver and more confident than before.
Despite this, Asa can be falsely self-assured and overconfident, such as her belief that she would easily be able to seduce Denji.
For example, she believes that giving Denji long lectures about ocean facts on their aquarium date would be a great way to win his affection.
For example, she doesn't feel bad about having accidentally killed Bucky, but feels bad because of the looks her peers gave her.
Her body physically forces her to trip during pivotal, high-stakes moments where success and happiness are close.
Her moral compass is somewhat artificial, as she is often more worried about the consequences certain actions carry instead of the actions themselves.
Her personality shifts from the cynical, deeply depressed, and socially reclusive girl burdened by Yoru to a much brighter and more well-adjusted teenager.
However, this was short-lived as she easily fell back into depression and even attempted suicide during the Falling Devil fight.
Instead of acknowledging that she intentionally delayed, she rationalized that she was simply "clumsy" and "incompetent".
Once she does make a mistake, however, she usually gets very angry and blames everyone around her except herself.(Chapter 113)
Over time, Asa becomes a skilled manipulator, coercing Katana Man to betray Public Safety by taking advantage of his hatred towards Chainsaw Man, claiming she wants to fight Chainsaw Man herself.
She also suffers from low self-esteem and considers herself to be clumsy.
She believes people only have sex when there's nothing better to do, and the thought of mixing her saliva and sweat with someone else sickens her.
She doesn't do so because it goes against her morals, but because she does not know what is right and wrong and constantly tries to avoid making mistakes.
She has a very negative outlook on the world, other humans, and Devils, and tends to assume the worst of others.
She is shown to have a negative opinion of sexual intercourse when Chainsaw Man reveals his main drive in life is to have sex, and she openly expresses disgust.
She is, however, very fond of cats and would rather kill a human than a cat.(Chapter 112)

She seeks validation, as shown by her internal monologue during her meeting with Hirofumi Yoshida, or breaking down and seeking comfort from Yoru despite being afraid and screaming at her mere moments prior.
She struggles with trust and fears being alone, yet also fears approaching others because she worries about making mistakes and ending up alone once more.
This also gets reaffirmed in the aquarium, where Asa refuses to kill Denji after being trapped and starved for several days.
This causes even Katana Man, with his unrivaled hatred for Denji, to insult her.
This puts her in a "cognitive dissonance", as she puts it, where she's afraid of both solitude and companionship.
Though after calming down, she'll break down in self-deprecating rants.(Chapter 115)(Chapter 121)
To cope with the overwhelming guilt of wanting her father dead and aiding in his demise, Asa's brain rewired the memory.
Upon Fami suggesting that food could change his demeanor, Asa asks Denji what he'd like to eat.
When he answers with sushi, Asa refuses since she can't stand seafood.
When the public gives her the recognition she yearns for, she initially claims to dislike being popular, but then smiles while watching people on TV praising her.

Augmented Body: Barem has strength, defense, and speed well above average for being a hybrid, being able to match beings like Katana Man and Chainsaw Man.
Blood Consumption: As a Hybrid, Barem is able to heal wounds by consuming blood, regenerating his entire body.
Even if he dies, as long as someone presses his molar, Barem can come back to life in perfect condition.

Flamethrowers: Barem can generate powerful blasts of fire from his flamethrowers; they are strong enough to cause explosions that reach an entire floor of a building and set an entire horde of zombies on fire.
He can survive being shredded, getting shot, and take all kinds of injuries that would kill most Devils.
Hybrid Transformation: By pressing down his molar, Barem can transform into a Hybrid with tanks for a head and flamethrowers for arms.
Nigh-Immortality: Due to being a Hybrid, Barem is immortal and nearly unkillable.
After joining the Chainsaw Man Church, he ties his hair into a ponytail and wears a white buttoned shirt with white pants and black suspenders.
Barem is a tall man with relatively long black hair that’s swept behind his ears, with the exception of one strand of hair that drops from his forehead and connects to his right eyebrow.
During his time as one of Makima's brainwashed servants, he wore a standard Devil Hunter uniform consisting of a suit and tie.
He keeps his black necktie, now tucked in the shirt's breast pocket.
His arms transform into giant flamethrowers that serve to attack his enemies.
When transformed, Barem has his head transformed into three huge fuel tanks while his neck becomes a jumble of metal parts.
After this revelation, he takes more outward delight in Denji's suffering, though he still admires Chainsaw Man and the powers of the Chainsaw Devil.

Barem believes that Makima could have defeated the Death Devil if she'd used Chainsaw Man's power and brought about a controlled, peaceful world, demonstrating that he agrees with Makima's plan and the "peace" it would've brought.(Chapter 151)
Barem has a very intense loyalty towards Makima.

Barem states that part of why he idolizes Chainsaw Man isn't just due to his love of violence, but due to how he's able to get back up again and fight despite no matter what is thrown at him.(Chapter 142)
Because Denji eliminated her, Barem holds him responsible for destroying the promise of peace Makima would have brought and holds that burning Denji's house was his punishment for Makima's death.
Despite his rudeness towards Denji, he does appear to genuinely admire and worship Chainsaw Man, seeing how far he's willing to go in order to see him transform.
Even after Makima's death and being freed from her control, Barem continues to worship her.
Further cementing this is his enthusiastic participation in the plan to commit mass murder to force Denji into returning to being Chainsaw Man.

He also appears to have a slightly juvenile and twisted sense of humour, doing things like teasing Denji about his supposed crush on Asa before making his threat, as well as by sticking his fingers in Denji’s nose as a greeting.
He does not hesitate to order Nayuta killed in order to get Denji to unleash his fury.(Chapter 147)
He justifies all of his misdeeds by blaming them on human nature, expecting God to ultimately forgive him.(Chapter 140)(Chapter 141)
He later abandons his plan to kill Asa Mitaka in favor of burning Denji's cat and dogs, since Denji is much more close to them, remarking that they are also more flammable.(Chapter 150)
He was shown to be observant enough to notice Pochita's weakened state, and displayed a rather manic side when blowing up an entire building using his flamethrowers.(Chapter 88)(Chapter 94)
In addition to this, he despises Denji for hypocritically living a calm and peaceful life after preventing Makima's own plans to bring peace.
Initially Barem's real personality was unknown, as he was brainwashed and mind-controlled by Makima.
This does not stop him from taking actions that would cause serious trauma to Denji for the sake of the mission.
This even extends to implicitly threatening Denji when attempting to force him to choose between his normal life or transforming once more.
When Nayuta attempted to use her abilities on him, he resisted and began strangling Nayuta, admitting that his heart still belongs to Makima and because of that, Nayuta could not control him.

When he makes a return in the Academy Saga, Barem's true personality reveals him as a psychopathic, cruel, and callous individual, as he casually suggests murdering Asa Mitaka for the sake of getting to see Denji as Chainsaw Man.

As a Devil, the Bat Devil possesses all of the standard devil abilities.
Following his latest reincarnation, he weakens and loses most of his unique abilities.
He also appears to have lost his intelligence, becoming a creature incapable of speech.
Since bats are usually associated with vampires and blood suckers, the Bat Devil is quite strong.
After drinking Denji's blood the Bat Devil was able to regrow his entire severed arm.(Chapter 6)
Bat Wings: The Bat Devil is able to extend his wings and fly through the air, despite his enormous size.(Chapter 7)
Blood Consumption: As a devil, the Bat Devil is able to restore his health by consuming blood.(Chapter 1)
He attempted to use it to destroy Denji in his Chainsaw Man form but Denji was able to regenerate from the damage.(Chapter 8)
He can fly very fast, crossing large distances in a very short period of time.
Mouth Cannon: The Bat Devil can compress his mouth into a gun-barrel shape that extends from his face, through which he can fire an immense blast of air pressure that can demolish buildings.
This ability likely comes from the fact that real bats are capable of echolocation.
Enhanced Smell: The Bat Devil has a keen sense of smell, being able to smell the various scents of humans in the city from a distant building.(Chapter 7)
After getting hit by a car thrown at him by Denji, The Bat Devil came out with only a few minor cuts.
Enhanced Durability: The Bat Devil was able to survive getting punched through walls and fall from the sky without suffering from any visible injuries.
Enhanced Strength: With a single punch, the Bat Devil can strike through and destroy the ceiling of a house, creating a hole for him to crawl through.(Chapter 6)
His strength is great enough to let him effortlessly pick up and throw a car with just one arm(Chapter 8) and fly through the air while carrying his enormous body without any issue.

His arms are connected to his torso by flaps of skin which also serve as wings.(Chapter 7)
His body has dark-purple coloration, though in the anime it is changed to a simplistic dark-grey.
The Bat Devil resembles an enormous humanoid bat with a grotesque face featuring multiple sharp teeth and large round eyes with a muscular body.

The Bat Devil then drinks some of Denji's blood and regenerates his arm and back.
The Bat Devil tries to fight back and blows Denji away with his attack, but Denji gets back up and continues fighting him.
Then they receive a request for devil-extermination for an unknown devil at the Morin Hotel and Makima's squad is dispatched for the task.
Then, using the situation, she requests from Denji to kill the Gun Devil.
Waking up in the hospital, Aki interrogates Denji about the events that occurred, but Denji protects Power.
As a Fiend, Beam can't make contracts with Devils and his powers are considerably weaker than those of his devil form.
However, he still has all the other standard devil abilities.
Devil Transformation: Beam can transform his head into an enormous shark's head with multiple eyes and great biting power.(Chapter 34)
He didn't seem to be able to bring others with him or bring large objects through.
Intangibility: Beam has the ability to swim through solid objects, allowing him to pass through walls and the floor with ease.(Chapter 34)
With his full transformation, Beam's entire body transforms into his Shark Devil form.(Chapter 49)
Enhanced Smell: Fitting for a shark fiend, Beam has a strong sense of smell.
He was able to recognize and correctly assume that Reze was a Bomb Devil hybrid based on her scent.

Enhanced Durability: Beam is very durable for a fiend, able to survive point-blank explosions caused by Reze multiple times and still have enough mobility to escape afterwards.(Chapter 49)(Chapter 50)
As a fiend, his shark snout and fin replace of the top half of his head; he has no visible eyes.
Beam possesses the body of a muscular young man.
He has short, spiky black hair and very sharp teeth.(Chapter 34)
In his full transformation, his entire body resembles a shark but with multiple sets of long fins that he uses as legs.(Chapter 49)
When Beam partially transforms into his devil form, his head becomes a massive shark head with three pairs of eyes.
Beam is very eccentric, naive and innocent.

He is shown to greatly enjoy fighting, eagerly diving into packs of zombies and eating them,(Chapter 34) though he was greatly afraid of having to fight against Reze to the point of fleeing, but showed no hesitation in trying to fight back against her when cornered.(Chapter 45)
He often goes along with Denji's plans no matter how crazy they are due to having a lot of respect for the Chainsaw Devil.(Chapter 49)
His devotion to Chainsaw Man is such that he always tries to protect Denji personally and will offer his blood to revive him, even if ends up severely hurting or killing him.
After Denji dives into the water to defeat Reze, Beam later dives in after him and rescues both of them by taking them to the beach.(Chapter 51)
After Denji is defeated by Reze, Beam and the Angel Devil restore him by feeding him blood.
After Power drinks too much blood in the attack on Akane Sawatari's hideout and has to be taken away temporarily, Beam is assigned to be Denji's partner at his own request.(Chapter 39)
As soon as he jumps away with Denji he realizes that Reze is the Bomb Devil hybrid by her smell.
Beam follows Denji around by swimming through the floor when they're out on patrol and is overjoyed when it rains.
Beam later intervenes to save Denji when Reze attacks him on their date.
Beam reveals how the Chainsaw Devil used to move around in the past by using the chains from his chainsaws to navigate through buildings.
Before Reze can finish him off, he swiftly escapes with Denji as a group of civilian devil hunters briefly distract her.(Chapter 45)
Denji tells him to stay out of sight because he'll cause a scene otherwise.(Chapter 40)
Denji then makes Beam transform into his full shark form and mounts him, using his chainsaw chains like reins instead of how Beam recommended.
He is very happy to be partnered with Denji and calls him Lord Chainsaw continuously.
He takes Denji to an Anti-Devil 2nd Division Training Center and informs Aki about the Bomb Devil, stating that she is the Gun Devil's ally.
He tries attacking her with his shark head attack but she quickly defeats him with a point-blank explosion.
He tries to dodge her attacks to no avail and is blasted back by her explosions.(Chapter 45)
Reze appears outside the building and Beam warns Aki that she's arrived.(Chapter 45)
Reze attacks from above and Beam puts Denji in his mouth to protect him, taking the brunt of the attack in exchange which incapacitates him.(Chapter 50)
Reze transforms and quickly catches up to him and Denji.(Chapter 44)
They manage to wound Reze, who recovers after drinking blood, and kill the Typhoon Devil after charging into his vortex and slashing him.
They move in to attack Reze and the Typhoon Devil together.(Chapter 49)
They then try to escape by car but Reze catches up to them quickly.(Chapter 46)
When Aki questions him on how he knows this, Beam claims he can't explain because Makima would kill him.
When Reze breaks Denji's neck and leaves, Denji begs Beam to rev his engine and heal him.(Chapter 51)
Beam is mentioned during the news broadcast by an interviewed woman who said she saw Denji riding him during the fight with the Typhoon Devil.(Chapter 89)
As the Darkness Devil arrives, it cuts off Beam's arms along with the arms of every other person present.(Chapter 64)
As the Darkness Devil begins slaughtering all of the humans, fiends, and devils present, Beam picks himself up and feeds blood from his stumps into Denji's mouth.
Beam advises Denji not to use his chainsaws so that he can save up his blood, but he trips over a doll's body as they're fleeing.
Beam assists Makima and the Spider Devil in cleaning up several doll puppets controlled by Santa Claus.

Beam is knocked unconscious by Tolka's attack and is dragged to Hell alongside everybody else in the department store after Tolka's master turns him into a perfect doll and summons the Hell Devil.(Chapter 63)
Beam watches this in shock until Tolka, who had been hidden nearby, stands up and kicks Beam in the face.(Chapter 62)
Denji calls him out on being clumsy but winces in pain as he stands on a nail; this triggers the Curse Devil who picks up Denji and causes him to begin bleeding profusely.
He appears in the department store where the fight is underway and rescues Denji from being pinned by Long by bashing her in the back with his oversized shark head.
He pulls on Denji's rope cord to revive him and begs him to grant their wish, moments before the Darkness Devil points in his direction and cuts Beam into pieces, killing him instantly.(Chapter 65)
He roars at her to not touch 'Lord Chainsaw' and he retreats with Denji.(Chapter 62)
Makima states she'll continue to clean up the situation and orders Beam to go assist Denji which he enthusiastically agrees to.(Chapter 59)
When he wakes up, Beam senses the presence of the Darkness Devil and panics alongside the other fiends as it approaches.(Chapter 64)
Beam is among the fighters from the Special Division 4 that are tasked with invading Akane Sawatari's hideout.
He almost accidentally bites through the Violence Fiend but is punched back by him and reverts to his original self.(Chapter 34)
He emerges from the wall below ground and dives into the pack of zombies, partially transforming his head into a shark head, and kills several of them with ease.(Chapter 34)
Beam derives his power from Selacophobia (or Galeophobia), the fear of sharks.
Beam fits within the sea-related devils alongside the Fish Devil, the Moray Eel Devil, the Octopus Devil and the Sea Cucumber Devil.
Beam is a fiend who visually looks like a human and animal mix along with being able to go in his full devil form both fully and partially, usually seen partially at the head.

Cherubs were originally depicted as humanoids with four feet and four faces of different creatures/animals including a that of man but would later on take the more famous baby-like and innocent appearance.

After being rejuvenated once more with help from the Angel Devil and Beam, Denji devises a new strategy to counter Reze by using his chains to ride on Beam's shark form.
Afterward, Denji and Reze rest in the classroom as it begins to rain.
Afterward, Denji asks Makima if he does have a heart, to which she confirms it by checking his pulse, leaving him in good spirits.
Aki is soon joined by Galgali, forcing Reze to call in the Typhoon Devil, who immediately begins causing havoc and chaos throughout the city.
Aki takes Denji to safety alongside the Angel Devil and Beam while Division 2 holds off Reze for the time being.
As Reze heads to the restrooms in good spirits, a serial killer emerges from the shadows and chases her onto the school's balcony.
As she loses consciousness, Reze recalls the reason she couldn't bring herself to kill Denji was because she empathizes with him for being unable to live a normal life.
As the two enjoy the peaceful evening, Reze makes up her mind and asks Denji to run away together.
At the café, a depressed Denji realizes Reze never arrived and believes she stood him up.
At the same time, a purple-haired girl named Reze approaches Denji inside the telephone booth.
Beam and Denji barely manage to evade her explosives as they arrive at Division 2's headquarters, where Aki and his old coworkers are spending time together.
Beam frantically informs the Devil Hunters that the Bomb Devil is in alliance with the Gun Devil but cannot say anymore as he promised Makima.
Before Reze can escape with Denji, Aki attacks her from behind to free Denji.
Before he can comprehend Pochita's words, Denji is suddenly uppercutted by Power, who is revealed to have drank too much blood from her battle with the Yakuza's zombies.
Before the deranged figure can kill her, Reze swiftly disarms him and slowly strangles him to death.
Before they fight, Denji expresses frustration that every woman he meets tries to kill him, wondering if any woman will see him for who he is.
Denji and Beam ride back into the fray for their rematch against Reze and the Typhoon Devil.
Denji and Reze eventually awaken on the beach, having been dragged out by Beam.
Denji complies and slowly realizes that he now has feelings for two women: Reze and Makima.
Denji doesn't respond as he bluntly devours the bouquet, much to Power's annoyance.
Denji is initially confused but Reze tells him she loves him and promises to protect him from harm.
Despite this, Denji turns down Reze's offer as he still wants to continue his job and visit her from time to time.
Disappointed, Reze attacks Denji and prepares to take his heart out by force.
During one of the movies, Denji notices Makima tearing up over an emotional scene, a rare moment of vulnerability from the emotionless woman.
Elsewhere, Reze changes her mind regarding Denji's proposal to run away together and heads back to the café.
Elsewhere, the Angel Devil informs Aki the origins of the fable and admits that he prefers being the country mouse to avoid being further involved in the city's dangers.
Following his victory over Katana Man and his Yakuza, Denji awakens from the same cryptic dream in which Pochita warns him to never open the door he's standing behind, no matter what.
From there, Denji tries the bitter taste of coffee for the first time, while Reze promptly introduces herself after learning his name.
Getting back up, the unfettered Reze coldly tells the Typhoon Devil to dispose of the serial killer's corpse before heading back to check on Denji.
However, touching the Angel Devil reduces his lifespan by two months.

In the aftermath of Reze's attack, Kishibe tells Aki of an urban legend regarding the Soviet Union and reveals that Reze was one of the children experimented with by the Soviets to serve the government's needs.
Inside an undisclosed school, Reze guides Denji through the hallways and teaches him simple subjects such as grammar and mathematics.
Knowing that she cannot use her powers underwater, Denji restrains Reze with his chains and throws the both of them into the ocean.
Makima sends Power to have her blood drained and decides to pair Denji with the Shark Fiend Beam.
Meanwhile, Aki Hayakawa and the Angel Devil are partnered together as buddies, but the two are unable to get along initially due to their differing views on handling their duties.
Not too long after, Reze arrives at the headquarters, ready to cause another massacre.
On the day of the festival, Denji and Reze spend time playing various games, eating food, and eventually watching the fireworks at a nearby fence.
Out of nowhere, Beam quickly grabs Denji and carries him to safety.
Over time, Denji and Reze begin spending more time together as he starts visiting her more often.
Power suddenly barges in and asks Denji if the flowers he has are for her.
Pulling the grenade pin on her neck, Reze transforms into her Bomb Hybrid form to give chase.
Regardless, the Typhoon Devil meets its end by Denji, who ends up cornered by Reze after she takes Beam out of the fight.
Reze asks Denji whether he prefers to be the town mouse or country mouse, to which he chooses the town mouse, as he prefers food and fun over safety.
Reze declines the offer but Denji promises to wait for her at the café at noon.
Reze manages to catch up to Aki's group after slaughtering Division 2, only to be stopped by Galgali and Kobeni.
Reze returns to the café and readies herself to work, only to find Denji already seated at one of the tables.
Reze reveals that her feelings for him were nothing but a ruse, but Denji asks her to run away with him.
Reze tells Denji she does like him but Aki shoots down that claim.
Reze thanks Denji for the flower and asks him to come visit her at the café she works at.
Seeing that Denji is annoyed by Beam's enthusiastic demeanor, Makima proposes a date with him for the following day.
Seeing that is what Denji prefers, Reze proposes to meet up again the next day at a festival to have more fun together.
She also expresses concern upon learning how Denji lives out his life working under Public Safety.
The Angel Devil is nearly sucked into the Typhoon Devil's swirling body but Aki saves him, not wanting anyone else he cares about to die again.
The two Hybrids engage in an explosive battle that ends with Reze overpowering Denji using her explosives to brutally subdue him.
The two decide to go swimming in the school’s pool, where Reze helps Denji learn how to swim.
The two reminisce about their time swimming together before losing consciousness.
The two spend their date together by having a non-stop movie marathon until midnight.
This diversion gives Denji enough time to recover and transform before confronting Reze directly.
Unbeknownst to the two, a serial killer working with the Typhoon Devil plans on targeting Reze to lure Denji out for his heart.
Wanting to impress Reze, Denji decides to perform a magic trick by pulling out a flower from his mouth, having obtained it earlier from a charity event.
While Denji and Reze go all out against each other, the Typhoon Devil's swarming mass of flesh tears up the battlefield.
While grabbing lunch, Reze learns that Denji has never gone to school and asks him to explore a nearby school with her at night.
While patrolling in the daytime, Denji finds himself running into a telephone booth to avoid getting drenched by the sudden rain.
With help from the Angel Devil, Makima subdues Reze and seemingly kills her.
As a Devil, the Chicken Devil possesses all of the standard Devil abilities.
However, since chickens are not very frightening to humans, Bucky is not very strong.
Unlike the superficially similar Pig and Fish Devils, Bucky has a normal human-level intelligence and the capacity for speech which allows him to interact with humans.
Chicken Wings: The Chicken Devil has a pair of white-feathered wings on his back, which he can use to fly.(Chapter 232)
Bucky appears as a headless chicken with a bow tie.
He is able to speak despite his obvious lack of a head.
Despite being a Devil, he shows absolutely no antagonism or hostility to humans, though he does mention he’d have no hope of surviving on his own, which may hint at the pragmatism of being friendly.
At some point, Tanaka captured or otherwise acquired Bucky to become a class pet.
Afterward, it was revealed that the Class President tripped Asa under orders from the "Justice Devil", and make Asa take all the blame for Bucky's death.(Chapter 98)
Asa Mitaka tried to carry him to join in at recess due to him remembering her name, giving her clarity that the class does care for her.
At Fourth East High School, Mr. Tanaka presents Bucky as a class pet, telling the students that in 3 months, they would kill and eat him.
Bucky would later be buried, and Asa became a victim of her classmates' bullying due to this incident.
However, Asa trips and falls on top of Bucky, collapsing his torso and exposing his entrails.

Over time, Bucky became a beloved pet to the class, and at the deadline of his death, they refused to kill him, despite him being a Devil, to Tanaka's elation, saying the real lesson was to value all life.
After Pochita erases himself and brings upon a new reality, Bucky is brought back to life.
After being fatally wounded by Yoru, Denji desperately attempts to regenerate from his injuries as he drags himself to safety.
As she lays bleeding, Yoru questions in irritation as to why she isn't healing.
At the last moment, Denji suddenly regurgitates a dove, causing Yoru to subconsciously relive the grief of what Asa felt when she accidentally killed Bucky.
Closing in, Yoru gives chase and promises to tear Denji to shreds with her Chainsaw Motorcycle.

Denji explains that although her contract with the Governor of California makes California civilians to shoulder any fatal attack dealt to her, self-inflicted injuries — such as when she crashed into the school building — do not work the same way.
He is seen with Asa at Fourth East High School.
Knowing that Asa hates seeing birds get killed, Yoru immediately swerves away from Denji's path and crashes into a building, hurting herself in the process.
Once Denji prevents Asa from tripping and falling on Bucky, she thanks him for dealing with the hostile Devil minutes ago.
She asks Yoru why she avoided hitting the pigeon, to which the latter responds that she could not bear to make Asa relive that pain again.(Chapter 228)
With that, Asa runs off to join her classmates with Bucky accompanying her.(Chapter 232)
Yoru then sees Asa standing before her as she bleeds out.
Bucky derives his power from Alektorophobia (from Greek ᾰ̓λέκτωρ: "rooster"), an intense, uncontrollable fear of chickens or hens.

As a Devil, the Car Devil possesses all of the standard devil abilities.
Besides those, not much is known about the Car Devil's abilities.

However, Makima considers the Car Devil as relatively powerful despite cars not being inherently frightening but are often associated with the fear of traffic accidents, being struck by a vehicle, and the potentially fatal consequences of automobile collisions, all of which contribute to the fear surrounding the concept of cars.(Chapter 6)

As members like Nobana Higashiyama and Seigi Akoku never turned into copies of Chainsaw Man, it can be deduced that there are likely many members of the Church who never contracted with the Fire Devil or who never had the wedding that sealed their fate.
For this reason, it was initially translated as "Chainsaw Man Society", but then became "Chainsaw Man Church", with the initial mention being reedited after a few days.
Haruka Iseumi didn't get turned either, so it's possible "Fami" spared them, as they were members of the same Devil Hunter Club beforehand.
However, rather than being anti-communist and focusing its efforts on Korean Unification, the Chainsaw Man Church is instead anti-American, and it's focused on preventing the Prophecy.

Interestingly, the "Chainsaw Man Society's" High School chapter was first mentioned by Haruka in Chapter 115, which is most likely the Devil Hunter Club, while other chapters, like the Chinese and Canadian, served as locations for transforming the people into Pseudo-Chainsaw People, as revealed in Chapter 146.
It's possible the Chainsaw Man Church was formed on 12th May, as a poster in Chapter 98 says a Chainsaw Man calling party has been made, calling forth all Chainsaw Man fans for a gathering.

The Chainsaw Man Church shares many elements with the new age Unification Church movement, such as their full names advocating for world peace, their prolific mass-weddings, their proclivity to perform questionable practices despite their good intentions, and their worship of a physical messiah figure.

The organization is consistently called the "Chainsaw Man Kyōkai", but the written kanji for the last word is "協会 (organization/association)" when it's first mentioned in Chapter 132, then "教会 (church/congregation)" afterward.

A contract is a supernatural agreement that compels its participants to fulfill its terms.

Although they cannot sacrifice someone unrelated to them, they can incapacitate someone else to offer them to a Devil, as seen when Santa Claus is able to offer an incapacitated Denji by bringing him to Hell with one of her perfect dolls which also indicates that a proxy is adequate to perform legitimate contract.
By sacrificing something the Devil finds valuable and will cause suffering, humans are able to use the supernatural abilities of contracted devils.
Contracts are binding in nature and cannot be broken on pain of death.
Contracts can only be formed between devils and humans - two devils are incapable of forming a contract with each other, with fiends being considered devils.
Despite this it is implied that an "exit clause" of sorts can be added for peaceful termination of the contract, seen when the Fox Devil terminated their contract with Aki yet neither died.

Devil Hunters tends to hide the details of their contracts and the abilities of their contracted devils to prevent their enemies from learning their weaknesses and strengths, as shown by Kobeni Higashiyama.
Devils are able to take their sacrifices by seemingly making them vanish instantly, as seen when the Ghost Devil takes all of Himeno.

Humans and their contracted devils can communicate with each other by being summoned as seen with Aki Hayakawa and his contracted devils, the Curse Devil and Future Devil, and with Himeno when she talked to the Ghost Devil's hand.

Humans can sacrifice anything they own: their body parts, senses, lifespans, legal children(Chapter 83) or their legally responsible individuals (for governors etc.) by verbally accepting or offering the terms.
It is shown that a human may be deceived as to the identity of their contracted devil which has no effect on the contract; as long as both abide by their terms the contract is valid.
It is shown that in Japan only Devil Hunters, either private or from Public Safety, can legally make contracts; presumably, similar policies are in place around the world.
It is unknown what happens to a sacrifice after being taken; though Himeno's "easy revenge" cigarette implies they aren't simply destroyed.
Pingtsi is able to see what Devil contracts a human has by transforming her futakuchi-onna-like hair ponytail of hers into a monocle/magnifying glass and looking through it.
Sacrifices can also be taken regardless of distance, as seen when the Hell Devil took Santa Claus' children while they were in Germany.
The formation of a contract seems to need explicit confirmation about its nature, particularly using the word "contract" in the terms.
They can also learn how much of a sacrificed resource they have left, such as lifespan, if that is the cost of the contract.
When a devil offers a contract to a human and the human accepts, neither can go back on their word.(Chapter 17)
Others are more permanent, with the human being able to access the devil's power by paying a one-time only price or by sacrificing something for each time the devil's power is used.
Some contracts only stated that the devil must do something in exchange for a price, and afterwards there is no lingering connecting between the devil and the human.
There are multiple ways a contract between a human and a devil can manifest.
A person's own individual devil transformation can look unique even if those individuals contracted with the same exact devil.
A type of contract where a human can gain a monstrous or very inhuman form is called a "devil transformation".

As devils fused into hybrids will gain a mostly permanent fusion with the human who became one, devil transformations seem to be a human's own transformation derived from the devil they contracted with but without the same exact function or triggers shown like a hybrid.

However, the encounter with the Fake Chainsaw Man proves that humans transformed into devils can turn back into humans and have their consciousness restored by controlling the devil's power that transformed them.

It is unknown how many people with a devil transformation can easily turn back into their human form as Yuko said that she became a "devil" and was trying to find her devil hunter relative who she said can turn her into a human again.

The people who have devil transformations that we've seen so far are: The Yakuza's contracts with the Zombie Devil, Santa Claus' contract with the Doll Devil and the Darkness Devil, the Class President, Yuko, an unnamed elder, the Fake Chainsaw Man and the Chainsaw Man Church's members' contracts with the Fire Devil.
This appears to be different from the contract with hybrids and the forms that have been seen appear even more inhuman than them.
After the process is done, the human gains the ability to transform into a Devil by activating a specific trigger located somewhere in their body.
Denji is the only known individual that has become a hybrid through a contract.
In rare cases, a devil and a human can fuse and give origin to a hybrid.
This process can be done through a contract, however it is very rare since few Devils would be willing to give up their consciousness to fuse with a human.
A type of contract where the human can summon the devil and employ them in combat.

With a few exceptions, these types of contract require that the human must pay a price for each time the devil is summoned, plus an additional price may be required if the human wishes to use a specific power from the Devil.
Both Aki and Santa received nail-like objects after making a contract with the Curse Devil.
In some cases, the power that a human receives from a devil manifest itself in the form of an object.
This object contains the devil's power and can be used to access it or to summon the devil himself.
