Katana Man uses his sword-dash move, but he gets killed by Pochita mere moments later, prompting Makima to say that the battle is unwinnable.
Kishibe is shown sitting next to him and asks him if he's Denji or the Chainsaw Devil to which he answers with a peace sign.

Kishibe prepares to shoot at Makima with his gun, but she says it's meaningless as she has a contract with the Prime Minister of Japan and all her injuries get transferred to people with Japanese citizenship.
Kishibe takes Denji and Kobeni to a discreet location.
Kishibe then comes and picks them up.
Kishibe then says she's the reincarnated Control Devil who he brought over from China.
Kobeni asks Kishibe if she's not going to see her family anymore as Makima's alive, to which he says yes.
Kobeni is relieved as a confused Denji doesn't understand her words.
Kobeni then tells Denji that there isn't a life free of bad things except in your dreams, which makes Denji stand up on his feet again.
Later, Denji is shown in a graveyard, sitting on a cross as he's awaiting Makima and her squad.
Makima asks Denji what he wants in exchange for defeating the Gun Devil, then Denji answers that he wants to be her dog.
Makima deems his current form unworthy as she commands her squad and the zombies to attack him.
Makima gives Denji tea and a dessert, after which Denji responds by saying that this is the best place in the world.

Makima reminds Pochita of his battle with the Four Horsemen and the Weapon Devils, where he vanished without a trace and was living in a near-death state and unable to be found even with all her searching.
Makima says her dogs should follow her with complete obedience and tells him that she invited Power over as it's his birthday.
Makima says she's a fan of his and reveals his identity as Chainsaw Man, "The Hero of Hell".
Makima then revives him by feeding him her blood and says that she will kill him herself.
Makima then shoots Power while saying "Bang", killing her.
Makima then uses the Zombie Devil, turning the devil hunters into zombies and attacking Power, while Makima blasts her with her finger bangs.
Makima uses Angel's 1,000-year usage to launch a spear directly at Kobeni, as Pochita takes the blow himself, protecting her, while Makima gets disappointed at how fast she defeated him.
Makima uses her finger bang attack, sending Pochita to space where he removes his heart and throws it back to Earth, while regenerating his entire body.
Pochita goes to a rooftop where he is met by Makima and her Special Division 5, who are tasked with eliminating Pochita, so Makima can take control of him.
Pochita heard Kobeni's cries for help in the Family Burger Restaurant and goes inside the restaurant, killing most of the staff present there.
Pochita returns to Kobeni's location and Makima soon follows, taking control of many of the Devil Hunters present with her chains.
Pochita takes control of Denji's body, turning into his Full Devil Form and slices the Hell Devil to pieces.
Pochita then takes Kobeni on a date and makes her dance, where she gets a perfect score.
Pochita wakes up Power, who's inside his body as Denji drank some of her blood beforehand.
Power defies Makima as she thinks of her friendship with Denji and runs away with him, while slaughtering multiple devil hunters in her way.
Power gives Denji her blood in exhange for finding her and making her Power again.
Power scolds Denji and tells him that she will revive in Hell but she won't be herself anymore.

Quanxi fires arrows at him, as the zombie army clashes with him and Barem uses his flamethrowers to scorch him, but he retaliates by jumping from the horde of burning zombies and slicing his head in half, while Quanxi, Makima's last line of defense, protects her.

Reze transforms into her Bomb Hybrid form, Katana Man transforms into his Katana Hybrid form, Miri Sugo transforms into his Longsword Hybrid form, Barem Bridge transforms into his Flamethrower Hybrid form, Quanxi transforms into her Bow Hybrid form and the Whip and Spear Hybrids transform as well.
She eats a piece of Pochita and manifests from inside his body, emerging in her Blood Devil form.

She explains his ability to erase devils from existence and wants to use his power to enact a perfect world, where adverse such as Death, War and Hunger don't exist, as she plans to erase them with Chainsaw Man's power.
She explains that she wanted to break his contract with Pochita, so she reveals to him that he murdered his father and takes control of Denji.
She introduces Denji to his followers in the hallway and says they have all been waiting for his resurrection, as Kishibe commands the Anti-Makima Squad to fire.
She orders Denji to open the door with the intention of killing her, as he remembers Pochita telling him to never open the door in his dream.
She pierces Makima and the Devil Hunters present with her blood swords and spears.
She tries smoking a cigarette while admiring Chainsaw Man and talking about how they're always going to be together.

Some time later, at a park, Denji takes Makima's dogs and Meowy on a walk as he sits to talk with Kishibe, explaining how he defeated Makima, saying that he didn't perceive eating her as an attack as it was a form of love, according to himself.
Spear follows suit, stabbing Denji, as do Reze and Whip, but he slices them up in a similar manner.
Suddenly, a small child bites Denji's finger, while he immediately recognizes her bite, exclaiming "Miss Makima".
The Hell Devil regenerates after drinking a devil hunter's blood and casts Pochita into Hell.
The Special Division 5, consisting of the Hybrids, under Makima's control, prepare to engage in a battle with the Chainsaw Devil.
The forces sacrifice themselves to summon the Hell Devil and cast Makima into Hell, as Makima calls for Chainsaw Man to save her.
Their conversation comes to a halt as Pochita emerges from the door to Hell.

Then, in a sudden twist of events, the real Denji emerges from the corpses nearby, surprising Makima and slicing her with a Blood Chainsaw, which he made using Power's blood to disturb her regeneration.
They engage with the Chainsaw Devil while flying through multiple buildings and destroying them in the process, while he kills Miri Sugo and Quanxi.
When inside, he is also met by a bunch of dogs.
While hesitant, Denji asks about her name, to which she responds as, Nayuta.
While in the sky, Pochita slices Reze to pieces, while Spear attacks him by throwing a spear high in the sky, piercing Pochita.
While outside, he's met up by Makima, who invites him to her apartment.
With his newfound popularity and courage, he devises a plan to take out Makima.
As a Fiend, Cosmo can't make contracts with Devils.

As the fiend that embodies the fear of the infinite knowledge of the cosmos and outer space, the more fear people have towards gaining total understanding of everything in the universe and similar concepts, the more powerful Cosmo will become.
However, she still has all the other standard devil abilities.

Cosmo may only be able to think completely normally when she is inside her own dimension talking to someone else that she sent there, but she does have a higher degree of functionality than her victims even outwardly, as she is not rendered semi-catatonic by her power.

However, due to the fact that Cosmo herself appears to be affected by her power, likely because of her weakened state due to being a fiend, she is unable to utilize or access this knowledge in any meaningful way, being only able to think and say the word "Halloween".
It is heavily implied that the target needs to copy Cosmo saying “Halloween” after she says it, and possibly for there to be some kind of direct focus, in order to work.
Omniscience: Cosmo has all the knowledge of the universe inside her head.
Once this occurs, the victim will be unable to think or say anything other than the phrase "Halloween" until their death.

She doesn’t seem to be omniscient when she isn’t using her ability, as in many circumstances she seems to not know or expect many things and, in contrast to her neutral inner personality, who accepts the fate of hunting or be hunted to be natural, seemed more concerned with death and freaks out in dangerous situations.
She would then force the target to understand everything in the universe.
This essentially gives her a possibility to be omniscient.
This is evidenced when a server at a restaurant was able to say words other than Halloween despite Cosmo using her ability on him, and when Quanxi told Cosmo to give Santa Claus an all-out Halloween.
This renders them into a semi-catatonic state in which they are "only able to think of Halloween until they die."
Total Understanding: Cosmo can telepathically send a person’s mind into her own mind, which seems to be a dimensional space that resembles a gigantic library.
What's more, Cosmo seems to be able to control the degree of her power and how much knowledge she infuses into her victim.
Cosmo possesses a corpse with spiky pink shoulder-length hair fashioned into pigtails with red hairbands.
It is inconsistent how much her right eye sticks out but it is probably retractable, as in one instance it seems as if she can move the eye on its own.
She also has hearts for pupils, colored either orange-red or yellow-red, and her right eye usually hangs out of its socket.
She wears a long sleeved cropped orange sweater, light blue high-waisted shorts, and pink sneakers.
The trailing part of her brain is tied into a bow at the end.
The upper right side of her head is gone, exposing her brain, part of which trails down past her face.
Cosmo was not particularly upset about her girlfriends' murders, explaining that she has no emotions strong enough to drive her to be upset about "the course of nature".
Her surface personality might be the result of her powers affecting her, causing her to only say "Halloween."
Her true personality therefore seems more logical, detached from others, and mostly devoid of emotion.
Here, she is capable of talking normally, conversing with Santa Claus about what's happening.

However, unlike those she inflicts her power upon, Cosmo is still capable of understanding the speech of others and seems to be capable of thinking, as she is able to take orders and carry them out just fine.
On the surface, Cosmo doesn't exhibit many emotions aside from her usual smiling, happy-go-lucky attitude.
She doesn't speak except for repeating the word "Halloween" and, like the rest of Quanxi's fiends, follows Quanxi around and is in constant love with her and under her command.
She is straightforward and formal in her manner of speaking, seeming far less excitable than her outward personality.
When Cosmo uses her powers on Santa Claus, the two had a conversation in Cosmo's mind, revealing her true, inner personality.

As revealed by the scarred Public Safety agent during Asa Mitaka and Fami's assault on the Tokyo Devil Detention Center, Quanxi was supposedly recruited into Special Division 7 with the promise of regaining the corpses of her now deceased friends and lovers.
The corpses of Cosmo and the other Fiends were eventually taken into custody by the Public Safety.
After Santa Claus kills Quanxi's other girlfriends besides Tsugihagi and threatens to make Quanxi one of her dolls, Quanxi tells Cosmo to give Santa Claus a taste of an all-out Halloween.
Cosmo explains that while she has no personal anger towards Santa Claus, the attack that will be launched on Santa Claus' mind is simply the natural order.
Cosmo is shown as one of Quanxi's girlfriends, alongside Pingtsi, Long, and Tsugihagi.
Cosmo obliges, and brings Santa Claus into her mind telepathically.
Cosmo then responds in normal speech to introduce herself as the Cosmos Fiend, surprising Santa Claus.
Despite her help in defeating Santa Claus, Cosmo is still beheaded by Makima along with Quanxi and Tsugihagi.
Like the other fiends, she is loyal to Quanxi and can be seen following her around during the arc.
Santa Claus observes that Cosmo intends to launch a psychological attack on her, but alleges that it would be ineffective.

She further tells Santa Claus that she is about to gain total knowledge of everything in the universe, and afterwards, she will be incapable of thinking about anything other than Halloween until she dies.
She never says anything other than "Halloween."
This is exactly what happens, and Santa Claus and all of her dolls are left semi-catatonic, only saying and thinking of Halloween.

Although Cosmo’s name suggests that she derives her power from the fear of space, also known as Astrophobia (the kanji "宇宙, Uchū" can also be translated as "universe"), it seems that she more fittingly embodies Gnosiphobia, or the fear of knowledge.
But it is unknown if her personality will also reset, as each incarnation of the same Devil is a different person.
Cosmo ranked 20th in the Second Popularity Poll with 3,527 votes.
Cosmo ranked 29th in the Third Popularity Poll with 2,943 votes.
Cosmo's name wasn't revealed before the Character Popularity Poll, in which she is referred to as Zombie ゾンビ Zonbi from Quanxi's group.
Cosmo's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: Cosmo ranked 34th in the First Popularity Poll with 343 votes.
Given the omniscient nature of her powers, Cosmo should be able to know and remember everything even after reincarnation.

It is unknown how or why the Cosmos Devil became a fiend, as her true personality reveals that she does not care about death, accepting it as a natural order that cannot be changed and was shown to be quite indifferent towards it, and unlike other Devils, she would not have to worry about losing her memories as knowing everything is a natural ability of hers.
After the attack, having no family left, Asa adopted the cat and named it Crambon.
Because of this, Asa's Mother had to stop and help her get back up.
During the attack of the Typhoon Devil, Crambon hurt its paw.
However, another orphan later told Asa that the children found Crambon drowned in a river.
It turned out that the caretaker had lied to Asa and killed Crambon because she was jealous that Asa still had someone she considered family.(Chapter 123)
Seeing this Asa tried saving it but tripped and fell.
There, her caretaker, whose mother also (allegedly) died because of the Typhoon Devil, convinced her to give Crambon away to give him a happier home.
Together with Asa, he was moved to an orphanage for children whose families have been killed by Devils.(Chapter 102)
Unfortunately, this ended up costing Asa's Mother her own life, devastating Asa greatly.
Crambon references Kenji Miyazawa's famous 1923 Japanese children's story, “Yamanashi” (The Wild Pear), where a crab brother mentions "Crambon" being killed under the water.
Crambon's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: Crambon ranked 64th in the Third Popularity Poll with 409 votes.
As a Devil, the Curse Devil possesses all of the standard devil abilities.
As a contract Devil, it showed its abilities based on its contracts.

As revealed by Santa Claus, the stabbing can also be done by another person, and not necessarily by the contractor themself as their contract was activated even when it was Tolka who stabbed Denji instead of them.

Curse: Upon its contractor stabbing their target a few times with its nail, the Curse Devil will manifest itself, pick up the target by their arms in a cross position, and mortally wound them by biting into their shoulders and necks while crushing their arms.
Each time he stabs his target, he shouts Fire!
In exchange for the loss of sensations on several of their fingers, Santa Claus can curse their targets by stabbing them with a nail 4 times.

Invisibility: When the Curse Devil appears, it appears to have the power to make itself invisible and not be seen by others, as when Denji was killed by the Curse Devil, neither he nor Beam could see the Devil, and it looked as if Denji being crucified while hovering in the air.
The contracts with it seen so far are: In exchange for some of his lifespan, Aki can curse his targets by stabbing them with his nail-shaped sword 3 times.
and a finger of the Curse Devil manifests to flick the nail.
In the anime, this was changed, with the Curse Devil physically appearing behind the one he speaks to.
The Curse Devil has clawed hands and a large, distended ribcage.(Chapter 24)
When summoned, the Curse Devil manifests as a large, two-headed skeleton with horns, its right skull appears human while the left skull has three eye slits and longer, mandible-like teeth.
Whenever it speaks to someone the Curse Devil appears as a dark pair of lips hovering in darkness or as a monstrously large mouth.(Chapter 24)(Chapter 29)
The Curse Devil's personality is currently unknown.
Aki Hayakawa considers using the Curse Devil's sword to defeat the Eternity Devil but Himeno restrains him with the Ghost Devil's arm.(Chapter 18)
If he succeeds then she will reveal her other Devil contracts to him.(Chapter 56)
She explains her contract with the Curse Devil to her apprentice and entrusts the fourth and final stab for him to perform as a test.
The Curse Devil appears and picks up Denji, violently biting into him and killing him.(Chapter 62)
Tolka lays a trap and manages to stab Denji by having him step on the nail.
Tolka's master uses a nail to stab Denji three times without him noticing.
Aki later asks the Curse Devil how much life span he has left after using the Curse Devil's power, and the Curse Devil states that he has two years remaining.(Chapter 29)
During his battle against Katana Man, Aki pulled out his Curse Spike to pierce Katana Man's body three times.
This trigger served to summon the Curse Devil on Aki's behalf who manifested behind Katana Man and picked him up before biting him and killing him.(Chapter 24)
In the anime, they suddenly appear from offscreen.
In the manga, the fingers used to flick Aki's sword appear from slightly outside the manga panels.
The Curse Devil and Taiyo Hayakawa ranked 62nd in the Second Popularity Poll with 1,279 votes.
The Curse Devil and Tanabe ranked 118th in the Third Popularity Poll with 71 votes.
The Curse Devil derives its power from Deprecophobia (from Latin deprecor: "curse"), the fear of curses and being cursed.
The Curse Devil's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: The Curse Devil ranked 43rd in the First Popularity Poll with 178 votes.
The Curse Devil's use of rituals involving nails is likely a reference to , a Japanese cursing ritual involving the insertion of a nail into a sacred tree or effigy.
Indeed, the Darkness Devil's power is such that ordinary Devils and humans will supposedly die the very moment they draw its hostility.(Chapter 64)

Naturally, it possesses all of the standard Devil abilities such as blood consumption, contract creation, etc. The only contract with the Darkness Devil seen so far was made by Santa Claus: in exchange for delivering the heart of Denji to Hell, Santa Claus gained a small piece of the Darkness Devil's flesh that allowed the assassin to manipulate their body in darkness and amplified their total power vastly.(Chapter 64)

The Darkness Devil is described as a transcendent being — one of the "Primal Fear" Devils that have never experienced death due to being so powerful; embodying such a concept, it can be assumed that the Darkness Devil is almost as old as humanity itself.
Blade of Darkness: The Darkness Devil can also conjure a large blade with bells attached to its hilt that can be telekinetically controlled to attack its enemies.
Darkness Manipulation: As the embodiment of fear of darkness, the Darkness Devil has the ability to manipulate darkness.
Devil Manifestation: The Darkness Devil appears to be able to forcefully manifest other Devils and kill them instantly.
Force Manipulation: The Darkness Devil has been shown to offensively manipulate an unseen force in various ways similar to the Control Devil.
However, Makima is shown to be stronger in this ability, as she can heavily damage the Darkness Devil only by pointing her finger at it.(Chapter 66)
Immense Healing Factor: While in the dark, the Darkness Devil can rapidly regenerate from any injury, easily healing from a powerful attack from Makima.(Chapter 66)
In the case of the Stone Devil, this also resulted in the death of the human they contracted with, Kusakabe.(Chapter 65)
It can also induce violent hemorrhages on those it watches.(Chapter 66)
It can transform into a mass of darkness and envelop the surrounding area in darkness, manifesting the bodies of 11 bisected astronauts as it does so.(Chapter 64)

It seems that the power of this ability can be increased by switching gestures, as the Darkness Devil completely twisted Makima's arm in the second attempt while praying with two of its hands despite the Control Devil trying to block the attack with all five fingers.(Chapter 66)
Nigh-Absolute Immortality: Devils of Primal Fear status are considered unkillable due to their power, hence why they never undergo reincarnation.(Chapter 64)
Once it makes contact, any being will hemorrhage violently once the bells ring.(Chapter 65)(Chapter 66)
Regeneration Nullification: Those who are dismembered by the Darkness Devil appear to have their regeneration nullified.
Shapeshifting: The Darkness Devil can transform its limbs into scythe-like appendages that can cut cleanly through opponents.(Chapter 65)
The Falling Devil affirmed that, at present, humanity has no means of attack that could kill a Primal Fear.(Chapter 125)

The extent of this ability is unclear, as Kobeni and Power were able to return to normal, only one of Aki's arms was reattached, and Angel's arms were permanently lost, with him stating that he is unable to regenerate them and can no longer be a Devil Hunter.

With this ability, the Darkness Devil can sever the arms of various humans, fiends and devils,(Chapter 64) cut them into pieces just by pointing at them(Chapter 65) or through movements of its many arms,(Chapter 65) or brutally obliterating their body after uttering an unreadable word.(Chapter 65)
By using its multiple arms it could slice through several fighters before they could react, and dodged or otherwise counteracted attacks with ease.
Immense Speed: The Darkness Devil can travel and attack at high speeds.
Immense Strength: The Darkness Devil has shown to be able to lift its targets with great ease and damage them easily by swinging its arms around.
It was able to appear in the midst of several Devil Hunters, including Quanxi, without any of them being able to perceive its movements.(Chapter 64)
Its head is akin to that of a pteranodon with curved horns.

The Darkness Devil's body is made up of many emaciated human bodies, with two bodies acting as its legs and four other human bodies acting as its torso, each having a unique face: the one immediately below the neck has no eyes, nose and a vertical mouth, the second head has open eyes and a stitched mouth, the third one has no nose, an open mouth and stitched eyes, and the fourth one has no eyes and a somber expression.
The first human body has its arms stretching outwards holding what seems to be a cape of darkness.(Chapter 64)
Even though it is almost entirely silent, it is shown to be intelligent and capable of reasoning, as a human can make a contract with it.
Like other Devils, it displays high animosity towards Chainsaw Man because of the threat he poses.
Nothing is currently known about the Darkness Devil's personality, except that it will attack anything it perceives as a threat.(Chapter 64)
As Makima's arm contorts and breaks, she offers Tolka's body to Hell Devil in return for bringing them back to Earth.
Beam successfully revives Denji by giving him his blood and pulling his chainsaw cord, but is sliced into pieces by the Darkness Devil.(Chapter 65)
Denji leaps in and unsuccessfully attacks the Devil with a chainsaw arm.(Chapter 65)
It emerges out of a door in the sky and immediately attacks, removing all of the group's arms.
It then kneels down over Aki Hayakawa and looks at him.(Chapter 65)
Just as it reaches down to grab Aki, Princi emerges from the ground nearby and unsuccessfully attacks the Darkness Devil, losing several of her limbs in the process.
Kusakabe tries to use the Stone Devil against the Darkness Devil, but is killed with the Stone Devil when the former seizes and destroys it.(Chapter 65)
Makima instructs Princi to summon her to Hell and she faces off against the Darkness Devil.(Chapter 66)

Quanxi and Tamaoki charge at the Darkness Devil simultaneously and try to kick it but the Darkness Devil swiftly scythes through them both, catching Long, Pingtsi and Power in the aftermath of its attack as well.(Chapter 65)
The Darkness Devil appears shortly after Denji along with several other Devil Hunters and assassins are transported to Hell by the Hell Devil.
The Darkness Devil clasps its hands together and Denji's body contorts painfully, disabling him.
The Darkness Devil conjures its black blade once more, and pierces Makima with it just as everyone is transported back to the department store.(Chapter 66)
The Darkness Devil fulfills its end of the request by feeding a piece of its flesh to Santa Clause on Earth.(Chapter 64)
The Darkness Devil looks at the Angel Devil and causes both him and Aki to start bleeding severely.
The Doll Devil, through Tolka, offers the Chainsaw Devil's heart in order to gain the power to kill Makima.

The Violence Fiend leaps in once more desperately with his severed arm held in his mouth, but the Darkness Devil summons a black blade which pierces the Violence Fiend and completely destroys his body.
The Violence Fiend, who has had his mask removed by Kobeni Higashiyama, leaps in from above to try and kick the Darkness Devil but is pierced multiple times.
The two of them point at each other; Makima's finger breaks and the Darkness Devil begins to bleed and stoops over.
With the contract complete, the Darkness Devil picks up Tolka and decapitates him.

Despite Santa Claus being accused of killing the people in the battle in Hell, even if she would not care if they were alive or not, it was the Darkness Devil who truly was responsible for their deaths as Santa Claus was only indirectly responsible.
It is also because frogs are synonymous in the dark, due to croaking most at that time which many considered to be malevolence.
The Darkness Devil derives its power from the fear of the dark, sometimes called nyctophobia, scotophobia (from Greek σκότος: "darkness") or lygophobia (from Greek λυγή: "twilight").
The Darkness Devil ranked 35th in the Third Popularity Poll with 1,889 votes.
The Darkness Devil's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: The Darkness Devil ranked 27th in the Second Popularity Poll with 1,575 votes.
The astronauts manifested by the Darkness Devil could be a nod to the humans who died in the darkest "realm" of the Darkness Devil: Space.
The frog's croak could be a reference to Kek - the Egyptian God of Darkness who had a head of a frog.
They pray in fear and represent the utter powerlessness of humanity in the infinite dark void of the universe.
While frog symbolism is tied to the fear of the unknown and the dangers lurking in the dark.
However, as a Primal Devil, it would likely be insufficient to kill them.

Light: Because Denji was able to overpower and damage a Darkness-empowered Santa Claus by lighting himself on fire (thus producing light and weakening the powers given to her by the Devil), it can be inferred that the Darkness Devil's powers can be counteracted with light.
After some thought, she decides to sacrifice a human who doesn't contribute to society, and upon noticing Denji and his self-centered antics, she settles on him.

After the chaos that occurred at Fourth East School, Asa Mikata is formally introduced to members of the Devil Hunter Club top brass, including Seigi Akoku, who lost his eye whilst trying to fight against Yuko, the club president Haruka Iseumi, as well as the mysterious hunter who resurrected Yuko.
Afterward, Denji walks Asa home, where he says he enjoyed their date, and invites her to a second one, to which Asa agrees.
As the two walk, they run into a group consisting of Haruka, Seigi, and an unnamed student, with Yoshida joining up with them immediately afterward.
Asa is then approached by Yoshida, who asks if she can keep him company for a bit.
Asa then gets the idea to collect money throughout the aquarium with Denji, and they amass over a million yen.
Back in the hallway, Haruka reveals to Asa that he is not Chainsaw Man but a super-fan of his.
Denji and Yoshida talk, and seeing no options left for them, Yoshida asks if Denji could eat the Death Devil.
Denji complies, and Nayuta erases Asa and Yoru's memories before sending them back to the school, making them believe he stood them up.
Denji finds Asa's reactions amusing, which cheers her up.
Denji finds Asa, who has retreated to a starfish tank and says she is hungry.
Denji returns and reveals that he believes the Eternity Devil has returned to trap them inside.
Denji warns Asa about the house rules he shares with his little sister Nayuta, one of which includes not kissing him.
However, the attempt fails, leading the two to believe he does not reciprocate.
However, when the time for the date comes, it's an utter disaster for Asa; Denji is bored to death by her endless facts and just wants to see the penguins, eventually walking off without her.
Nayuta agrees to turn "Asa" back only if Denji stops hanging out with her, wary of Yoru.

Now knowing their supposed target, Yoru tells Asa that in order to defeat him, she needs another strong weapon similar to her uniform sword, meaning she needs to sacrifice something she has an attachment to.

The group finds a staff lounge with plenty of water and food for supplies, though Asa's efforts to assist are unfruitful, as she ends up breaking her cell phone by accident, keeping the disappointed group isolated from the rest of the world.
The next day, after school, Denji proposes to go to a theater for a movie marathon, but after some discussion with Asa, they agree to go to his house to watch the movies on his VHS.
They get interrupted by Nayuta, who appears and uses her Control Devil abilities to make Yoru act like a dog.
To make matters worse, the mysterious hunter reappears and reveals herself as the Famine Devil to Asa, saying that she and Denji will be trapped until she can turn him into a weapon.
Using the money, Asa "buys" the aquarium, and using her guilt over ruining it, creates a powerful spear that defeats the Eternity Devil in one blow.
Yoru ignores this rule as she takes over Asa's body and kisses him, once again attempting to turn him into a weapon.
Yoru notices that Asa has developed feelings for Denji and takes the opportunity to turn him into a weapon.

Yoru takes over and asks Haruka if the rumors of the Chainsaw Devil being a member of the Hunter Club are true, to which he confirms by showing her a ripcord sticking out of his chest, in a similar way to Denji's.
According to Yoru, once Death descends, the other high-ranking Devils, such as the Fire Devil, will pay court to her.(Chapter 192)
Death herself possesses all the standard Devil abilities.

However, her sisters seem to believe that killing Death is within the realms of possibility: Makima desired to kill all her sisters by having Chainsaw Man eat them,(Chapter 84) and Death herself plots to empower the War and Chainsaw Devils by rapidly reigniting humanity's collective fear of them (by means of inciting a global war) so that both can grow strong enough to rival her.(Chapter 131)(Chapter 146)

However, rather than being directly involved in conflicts, she prefers to utilize the powers of other Devils who are either cooperating with her voluntarily or under her direct control, like the Guillotine Devil.
Indeed, the Prophecy of Nostradamus calls her "Ultimate Terror" and "Great King of Terror" — who is to usher in an Age of Devils and thus end the human race.(Chapter 122)(Chapter 131)(Chapter 146)
She is able to influence the power of Devils and is able to kill someone instantly by using her own powers.

She was able to separate Yoru from Asa temporarily but left Asa her power to turn people and objects into weapons and communicate with her at a distance despite Asa being trapped in another Devil's pocket dimension.
The Death Devil is the strongest Devil in existence, her name being the most feared of all.(Chapter 146)

The Death Devil likely draws on the fear from the Suicide Devil, since suicide is a concept related to death, the collective fear surrounding suicide likely heavily feeds into humanity's overarching fear of death.

While lesser "Primal Fears" are already transcendent beings that cannot be killed and whose mere presence can be felt across the world,(Chapter 64)(Chapter 135) the Death Devil's arrival is held as tantamount to the apocalypse.
While not fully awoken and not at full strength, she nonetheless demonstrates immense power over others.

Yoshida has reiterated this notion, stating that, while no country in the world has the means to prevent Death's descent, if War were to control Chainsaw Man as a mindless weapon, humanity may have a chance of surviving and perhaps even overcoming Death.(Chapter 191)
Absolute Immortality: Devils of "Primal Fear" status in general are considered unkillable due to their power, hence why they never undergo reincarnation.(Chapter 64)

A base aversion to death is ubiquitous in the animal kingdom and underlies many other instinctual fears like that of pain, predation, disease, starvation, etc. Predatory death anxiety, stemming from fear of harm, is the most primal death anxiety whose origins lie with unicellular organisms (e.g., protozoa) and their rudimentary, self-protective response mechanisms: their receptors evolved to react to stimuli to raise the likelihood of survival in the face of physical/chemical threats.
Because these birds are scavengers that appear on battlefields and near dead animals, they have long been seen as grim omens or "harbingers" of death.
Both Death and Justice are often represented by scales, which can be connected to how Asa originally speculated that she was the Justice Devil.
Death's earrings are likely a reference to the Horseman of Famine's depiction in the Book of Revelation, where he is depicted holding scales for weighing food.
Death's head is nearly always tilted to her left (like an unbalanced scale).
Existential death anxiety is thought to be the most powerful form, founded in the basic awareness of human mortality that arose in humans some 150,000 years ago and sets them apart from animals.
Famine is also sometimes interpreted as the "Lord as a Lawgiver".

Her earrings could also be interpreted as the scales of Anubis from the Book of the Dead, which shows Anubis performing a measurement that determined whether the person was worthy of entering the realm of the dead (the underworld, known as Duat).
Her tilted head gives her the appearance of having been hung from a noose, an image often associated with death.
However, others argue that the Prophecy was misinterpreted, with the "King of Terror" referring to something entirely different, like a political figure or a financial crisis.

In humans, aversion to death has been wired through millions of years of evolution, and particularly the predatory kind of death anxiety may be evoked by whatever scenarios put one at risk or threaten one's survival, usually triggering fight-or-flight responses.
Like with Santa Claus, Fujimoto likely gave Death numerous facial moles because he finds that the more moles a character has, the better they look.

Nostradamus' quatrain about a "great King of Terror" coming in the seventh month of 1999 was interpreted by some as predicting a catastrophic event, possibly linked to a solar eclipse, while others focused on the "King of Terror" being a specific individual or event.

Scholars distinguish various forms of death anxiety, like predatory death anxiety (fear of being killed), predator death anxiety (fear of taking another life), existential death anxiety, personal fear of death/the dying process or anxiety towards the death of someone close, fear of dead bodies (necrophobia), and so on.

She explained that without death as a "natural end" to life, creatures, including humans, continue to live, leading to situations where, for example, insects can overwhelm humanity and pests can eat people alive while they continue to suffer.(Chapter 230)
Similarly, the Death Devil has several motifs associated with the concept of death.
Since then (in a short span of evolutionary time), human psychology has fashioned a basic coping mechanism against this existential fear: denial.
The Death Devil has some similarities to the concept of "justice" represented in several ways.
The Death Devil is associated with churches as some religions center their core theology on mortality, resurrection, and the afterlife.
The Death Devil is strongly associated with crows and ravens, as they are culturally associated with the concept of death in folklore and mythology.
The Death Devil often appears on the ledges of buildings as if she's about to jump off, another image associated with death.

The Death Devil's earrings also bear a close resemblance to Chainsaw Man's pull cord and the way they are always tilted resemble a scale, reflecting the public's view of Chainsaw Man as a symbol of justice.
The Death Devil's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: The Death Devil ranked 18th in the Third Popularity Poll with 9,533 votes.
The Death Devil, being the third Horseman to appear, contrasts how, in Christian eschatology, Death is the final of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, riding the Pale Horse.

The notion that the Death Devil derives her power from "the ultimate fear" maps onto real life: fear of/anxiety about death and mortality (also called thanatophobia) is one of the oldest and most innate fears, if not the oldest.

The total solar eclipse that occurred on August 11, 1999 (July 29 in the Julian calendar), over Europe and parts of Asia, was seen by some as a fulfillment of the Prophecy, with the "King of Terror" being interpreted as either the eclipse itself or a figure associated with it.

Aging Devil Contract: In exchange for escaping Aging's World and never having to fight each other again, Denji made a contract with the Aging Devil.
All of his Hybrid abilities are originated from this contract.
Blood Chainsaw: Due to the blood gained from Power, Denji is able to manifest a chainsaw made from said blood, boasting a sharp pair of horns similar to that of Power's on the base of the chainsaw.
Blood Devil Contract: In exchange for finding the reincarnated Blood Devil and befriending them, Power gave all of her remaining blood to revive Denji.

By using her blood manipulation ability that was imbued into the chainsaw, Denji was able to disturb the contracted regeneration of Makima by causing her blood to continue ripping her body apart internally, which allowed him to defeat her.
Chainsaw Devil Contract: In exchange for living a "normal life", Pochita became Denji's heart and turned him into a Hybrid.
In the new reality created after Pochita erased himself, Power tells Denji that in exchange for saving his life with her blood, he now belongs to her as a human pet.
After being defeated by Makima to save Kobeni and later rescued by Power, Denji transformed back to normal and regained consciousness.
After losing his arm to Bat Devil, Denji's arm re-attached itself after he received a blood transfusion.(Chapter 11)

After noticing this method of regeneration, he is able to remove Pochita from his body and regenerate it as a separate entity that talked just like Denji, which allowed him to fool Makima, using the rest of Power's blood to seemingly keep himself alive without a heart while the duplicate fought.
As long as Denji continues to drink blood to recover from his injuries, he is essentially a perpetual motion machine.(Chapter 19)
Augmented Durability: While in his Hybrid form, Denji's physical durability is increased to inhuman levels.
Augmented Stamina: Denji was capable of fighting the Eternity Devil for approximately three days.
Augmented Strength: After entering his Hybrid form, Denji's physical strength is increased exponentially.
Blood Consumption: Denji is able to heal completely from nearly any fatal injury, and in some instances recover from death, so long as he consumes a sufficient amount of blood.
Body Duplication: As a full Devil, he regenerated from just his heart after he ripped Pochita out and threw it from space.
By extending the chains from a detached arm, he can latch onto surfaces or targets to propel himself away or drag his body across the ground.
Chain Entanglement: Denji is able to disconnect his chains from his chainsaws to use them in combat.
Chain Grappling: In his combined form, Denji is capable of using the chains connected to his chainsaws as grappling tools even when the limb wielding them has been severed.
Chainsaw Manifestation: As part of his transformation Denji grows fully-functional chainsaws from his arms, legs, feet and head.

Chainsaw Retraction: If he needs the full use of his arms and legs to do certain tasks while in his Hybrid form, Denji's chainsaws can be retracted into his body, allowing him to perform mundane actions such as grabbing objects.(Chapter 8)
Denji can also wrap his chains around objects to cut them, throw them or do both.(Chapter 94)
Denji needs blood in order to use his abilities, so if he does not have enough of it in his body, he can not fully transform and will instead enter a pseudo-hybrid form.
Devil Transformation: After surrendering his contract with Pochita, Denji transformed into a Full Devil.

During Denji's stay in the world the Aging Devil created he was still transformed into his Full Devil form, thus his stomach was connected to Pochita who was still in the real world, which allowed for Pochita to make Denji barf up people and Devils or for them to escape from his mouth.

During Pochita's battle with Yoru, Denji emerges from Pochita's body and claims that Pochita's strongest Devil powers have combined with his genius brain and thus, Denji transforms into a more powerful form capable of using Pochita's Devil powers.(Chapter 222)
Even after being decapitated, being cursed by the Curse Devil and having most of his body blown up, Denji still managed to come back to life with no lasting damage.
Even if he dies, as long as someone pulls the cord on his chest, Denji can come back to life in perfect condition.
He can break walls and kill most Devils with just one punch.
He can fall from great altitudes and punch Devils through walls, without receiving any injuries.
He can survive getting shot, being thrown from buildings and taking all kinds of injuries that would kill most Devils.
He can wrap his chains around his opponent's body and then pull them closer to him.
His head and chainsaws are far more durable than the rest of his body, due to being made of metal, and being capable of deflecting bullets.(Chapter 28)
His immense power is further highlighted in Hell, where it is implied that he defeated every Devil residing there.
Hybrid Transformation: By pulling on the cord emerging from his chest, Denji can transform into a bloodthirsty Chainsaw Devil.(Chapter 1)
If Denji runs out of blood, while already being fully transformed, his chainsaws will automatically retract themselves.(Chapter 19)
If Denji's arms get torn off but are still connected to his body, he can still use his chain like body tissue to wrap his enemies around.
In this form, Pochita displays incredible speed and strength, easily defeating multiple Hybrid Devils in a matter of seconds.
Just like the rest of his body, these chainsaws are regenerated every time Denji pulls his cord and fully transforms.
Makima stated that he has killed her 26 times in this form.
Nigh-Immortality: Due to being a Hybrid, Denji is immortal and nearly unkillable.

On one occasion, he was able to catch a thrown car out of the air without staggering and then throw it back with an equal amount of force(Chapter 8) and on another occasion, he was capable of lifting a car and then throwing it with enough force to make it explode.(Chapter 69)
The chains can also be used as grapple hooks, allowing Denji to wrap them around a target and then pull his body closer to said target.(Chapter 94)
The chainsaws in his legs and feet are not usually active, however, Denji can employ them just by willing it.
These chainsaws are extremely effective at cutting Devils' flesh, allowing Denji to sever limbs(Chapter 8) and bifurcate his enemies.
They are also very effective at cutting other materials, such as stone and concrete,(Chapter 94) however they have shown to be incapable of cutting through metal.(Chapter 78)
This form seems to lack Denji's personality and awareness, though it has been shown to retain some memories and frequently acts in accordance with them.
This is shown when Denji fires a chain from his severed arm to escape while retreating from Yoru.(Chapter 228)
Though he has been shown to have taken damage, and even been incapacitated by being sent to Hell and blasted into Space, these acts merely delayed him for a few minutes before he returned unscathed.
While Denji can willingly retract his chainsaws, they can also be retracted automatically based on his instincts alone.
While Denji still has access to some of his powers in this form, they are considerably weaker and his chainsaws are shorter.

While in this form Denji still doesn't posses Pochita's signature ability of Devil erasure which was proven in his fight against the Falling Devil which was eaten by him but neither weakened or erased.
With his fight against Santa Claus, he consumed one of her doll's blood to keep fighting while still being on fire.

Enhanced Endurance: Due to his rough childhood, Denji has developed a high tolerance for pain and stress, being able to still function as a Devil Hunter for the Yakuza despite having multiple of his organs missing at the time.
Enhanced Human Condition: Due to fusing with Pochita, Denji gained superhuman abilities even when not transformed.

His mental fortitude has allowed him to fight for three days straight while constantly being injured and remaining conscious even after having multiple parts of his body cut or blown off.(Chapter 19)

Denji was trained under Kishibe, who he refers to as "master" later on in the story, who teaches him various strategies.

He managed to use this skill to his advantage during his fight against her.

Strategic Intelligence: Despite never receiving a proper education, Denji is very perceptive when it comes to ascertaining his enemies' weaknesses and how to exploit them.

Denji's name is based on the Japanese word for angel, "Tenshi" (Denji: デンジ.
Fujimoto initially planned to name him Tenshi, but he decided to use the voiced versions of his name's consonants to make it sound more impactful (such as the impact in the word “danger”).
Tenshi: テンシ), which plays into the theme of several characters being named after different ranks of angels.
After becoming a Public Safety Devil Hunter and fulfilling his basic needs, Denji is unsure of what he wants in life.
Also, Denji has started to struggle with having a normal life since he has come to like transforming and being Chainsaw Man due to the attention and popularity he receives.

As he becomes increasingly jaded to living a normal life with constrictions on his personal freedom, his home burns down and his pets murdered due to the machinations of Barem, which finally pushes him over the edge.

As such, at the beginning of the second part, Denji's personality seems to have remained relatively stagnant, aimed at openly leaving clues that indicate that he is Chainsaw Man, such as leaving his school I.D.
As the story progresses, it becomes more evident that Denji is emotionally damaged, and desperate to feel love and be loved by someone.
Denji also harbors a fear that his seeming lack of empathy and attachment after his transformation is a sign that he is losing his sense of humanity.
Denji is both brash and naïve as a result of being unable to have a formal education and socialize due to living in severe poverty, making him generally crass and vulgar.
Denji told Aki that when he fights against men, he usually aims to their intimate zone (their testicles) and demonstrated it when they had a fight when he kicked him repeatedly in the groin.
Denji's constant repeats of making mistakes and getting traumatized has caused him a great deal of neverending misery.
Due to his desire to have intercourse with a woman, he generally treats women with more kindness and respect than men.
During the date with Asa, Denji becomes flustered and angry with her when she told him that he didn't need to think about anything, possibly reminding him of his relationship with Makima.
Furthermore, once he learns that he'd be forced to marry the girl with whom he'd have sex with, he draws a line and refuses to marry a random girl.
He also displays a twisted and sarcastic sense of humor.

He also expresses immense disgust at himself when he tries coping with the emotional turmoil that he feels over Nayuta's disappearance and the loss of his pets by trying to seek sexual gratification at a brothel, fully realizing that he constantly allows his base desires to supercede his priorities.

He also reveals himself to be obsessed with money, so much so that he is willing to let others pay to use him as a "chair" for a few yen (although he seems to enjoy it when a woman uses him as a chair) and to sell used cigarettes to the homeless, passing them off as new, just to make money.
He clings to Makima as a coping mechanism, even going as far as stating that his wish was to just be a mindless dog, so he would not feel hurt from losing the things and people he loved.
He displays practically none of the enthusiasm and upbeat demeanor he did before, and is constantly seen with a haggard expression and baggy eyes.
He does his best to treat women with respect and never does anything without their explicit consent.

He further reveals to Asa that the reason he is desperately saving money is to provide Nayuta with a proper education and a comfortable lifestyle, showing that he has acquired a strong sense of responsibility towards others.
He is able to clearly see that the anti-American conspiracy theory that they propagate is a lie.
He openly admits to Asa that he still hasn't gotten over his horrendous past.
He subsequently ignores Nayuta's pleas to run away with her and feels glad to be Chainsaw Man again despite the horrific circumstances that led to it happening.

All Devils can consume the blood of other creatures to heal their injuries.

However, this only works if the flesh/blood they ate came from a Devil that is still alive, as Denji did not get more powerful or gained the Control Devil’s ability, despite consuming Makima’s entire body.
It is also implied that Devils can grow more powerful by consuming blood.
The flesh or blood of a Devil can be fed to other creatures, making them stronger and even giving them the ability of the Devil they’ve eaten.
While all Devils can consume blood to quickly regenerate, powerful Devils have shown to possess better regeneration.(Chapter 39)(Chapter 1)
All Devils can make contracts with humans, allowing humans to borrow some of their power in exchange for a sacrifice.(Chapter 11)
However, Fiends are unable to perform contracts with Devils and Devils are unable to perform contracts with each other.
All Devils can also possess human and animal corpses.
In rare instances, Devils would deliberately like to retain the personality of the possessed corpse, effectively reviving them, and take over their personalities from time to time.
In these scenarios, the Devil may also retain some memories from the body they took over.
The only known instance of this happening is with the War Devil, who took over Asa Mitaka's body while keeping her ego intact.
The personality of the Fiend may mirror that of the corpse if the brain is still intact, as evident by the Violence Fiend's polite and gentle attitude.(Chapter 56)
This in most cases ends up creating a Fiend, though in rare cases it can end up creating a Hybrid instead under certain circumstances.

Devils are known to have a keener sense of sight, hearing and smell compared to humans, which allows them to track targets, detect approaching threats, and navigate their environments with supernatural precision.
All Devils are born with a "name" that ties them to a concept.

An example offered by Makima is how a Car Devil would be stronger than a Coffee Devil, since cars conjures up the mental image of getting run over and dying, while coffee does not evoke any scary ideas; another example is the Chicken Devil, which is so weak that it was kept as a class pet for a high school and killed when a student fell onto it.

As Yoru explained that the bulk of her power also comes from the fear the masses have towards Guns, Tanks and Nuclear Weapons, as fear of these weapons also leads to and includes a fear towards War, showing how collective fear towards specific concepts can empower a Devil whose concepts encompass a much broader concept.

As demonstrated by the War Devil’s connection to the Gun Devil, Tank Devil and Nuclear Weapons Devil, Devils whose concepts that also encompass the concepts of other Devils can also contribute to and increase a Devil’s overall power.
Because of this, a Devil's power is deeply related to how humans perceive the concept and the visual images that their "name" inspire.
Devils can also feed on the fear that other Devils have towards them, with the Chainsaw Devil managing to become extremely strong by using Devils' fear as his source of power.
Devils feed on the fear that humans and other creatures have towards that concept, gaining their strength from it.
In addition, the Chainsaw Devil removing certain concepts from existence can have a knock-on effect that empowers different concepts and Devils.

Pochita eating the Death Devil resulted in the empowerment of various Devils embodying pest species like insects, bats and cockroaches, as without death the offspring of these high fertility species aren't culled via natural selection and live forever, leading to rapid overpopulating and swarming the world consuming all life to fuel their own reproduction.(Chapter 230)

The fear that humans have towards Devils in general is also a source of power that they can utilize, since it was stated that after the Gun Devil attack, many Devils grew stronger due to people being more afraid of them generally.
The more fear is associated with a "name", the more powerful the Devil who possesses it becomes.(Chapter 6)
The power dynamic between Devils also means that closely related fears feed into one another.

This fear, pain and despair from humanity being eaten alive yet being unable to die by these swarms vastly empowered these associated Devils to the point where a single Devil, the Locust Devil, proved both a dangerous and overwhelming opponent for other strong Devils like the War and the Chainsaw Devils.(Chapter 226)
While the Suicide Devil's fear empowers it individually, collective, existential dread is exactly what makes the Death Devil the strongest and most untouchable force in existence.
Abilities / General Abilities / Flesh Power Boost
It is said that a Devil or human of any power can have their abilities boosted if they eat the flesh of a very powerful Devil, no matter what their original level of strength was.
Abilities / General Abilities / Flesh Power Boost

Some examples are the numerous Devils who became more powerful by eating the Gun Devil’s flesh, Santa Claus becoming a very powerful abomination after consuming the flesh of the Darkness Devil, and Power gaining her full Devil form restored from eating Pochita.
Another ability common among all Devils is reincarnation: when a Devil dies, they reincarnate in Hell; when they die in Hell, they reincarnate on Earth.
However, every time they reincarnate, their memories and personalities are reset, making them completely different individuals from their previous incarnation.
This ability makes them practically immortal.

According to Aki, a Devil's abilities are undone upon death,(Chapter 15) while Fiends can seemingly bypass this, as Cosmo's powers were active after her death and Power, in her Fiend form, was able to leave Denji her blood, which he used to make a Blood Chainsaw.
But it might not always or only apply to powerful Devils.

Despite each Devil has their own abilities, these may be common between different Devils or Fiends, such as Force Manipulation which used by the Control Devil and the Darkness Devil, or intangibility, which used by the Spider Devil and the Shark Fiend.
Devils also may possess other supernatural abilities correlating with their name.

Sometimes a Devil's natural ability or special ability may not always correlate or link up with what exactly their concept represents, or at the very least, won't represent a trait that is instantly known with the concept.
The conditions and effects of each supernatural ability is unique to the respective Devil.

The reason for these can be because of things like a more powerful Devil being able to have access to more abilities, like how the Snake Devil barely uses traditional snake ways of attacking, such as venom, but has shown "cheats" like consuming another Devil to make that Devil fight on their side.

If one consumes the fragment or part of a powerful Devil, either Devil or human, they will gain more strength than before.
It is possible for Devil fragments to be harmed, destroyed, and become Fiends on their own, yet for other parts of the main Devil to still remain alive and not destroyed.
It is unknown how many Devils have undergone fragmentation.
Presumably, a fragmented Devil cannot be fully killed and begin reincarnation until either all of its flesh pieces are destroyed or just their core.

Since the Gun Devil is the only example of extensive fragmentation and was more of a primal force than an intelligent being from the 20% of it seen, it is unknown if such Flesh Pieces retain the personality of the original, each have separate personalities, all lack distinct personalities, or if it varies from Devil to Devil.
According to the Angel Devil, him and the other Devils of Special Division 4 all remember the sound of the Chainsaw Devil's engine roaring before they died in Hell.(Chapter 53)
Another example would be the Blood Devil as most people don't fear blood itself, but they often fear the violent and gruesome imagery of blood and the danger of bleeding.
Devils are beings born from humanity's collective fear of specific concepts, all first manifesting in Hell.
Devils cannot recall any memories from their previous lives and their entire personality resets.
Devils manifest according to the collective consciousness surrounding their names (for example: the Gun Devil appears to be constructed out of guns and has gun-related abilities).
Devils that die in Hell reappear in the human world; Devils that die in the human world reappear in Hell.
Each name is unique to its respective Devil, though some overlap based on specificity is possible, as there have been both a War Devil and a World War II Devil.
For example, cars aren’t necessarily scary on their own, but Makima states that a Car Devil would be powerful because of the scariness of car crashes and other car-related incidents.
However, there are minor exceptions to this rule.
It is implied by the Falling Devil that animal fears play a role in a Devil’s power.
Rather its power relies on how much of a scary image it has in the popular consciousness of humans.
So long as the "name" of the concept still exists and is feared by the public consciousness, they continue to reincarnate.
The concept does not have to refer to something that exists; there is no indication that ghosts, zombies or angels exist in the world, yet all these names have corresponding Devils.
The concept of a Devil itself doesn’t have to be scary on its own nor does it have to embody a fear.
These can range from highly tangible (Fish, Tomato) to entirely abstract (Future, Curse).
They are born with a "name" that correlates to a concept.
They are the conceptual and physical embodiment of the "name" they represent.
All of these are known to have been incredibly powerful Devils before being weakened, so it is unknown if all Devils are able to assume a weakened state.
Devils also appear to be incapable of dying due to old age; they can live indefinitely until killed by external factors.
Devils do not reproduce as most organisms do, instead simply "appearing" in Hell.
Devils primarily feed on the blood and fear (or powerful negative emotions in general) of humans.

Devils who are friendly and are more inclined towards humans will take on a very humanoid form in the natural state of their incarnation, some being indistinguishable from a human save for some subtle tells.
Due to their nature of existence, Devils do not typically have familial relationships.

For that reason, while Devils and Fiends can also consume other kinds of foods, such as vegetables and fruits, most refuse to live off of them, since it will not heal their wounds or give them more power.
However they can also survive by drinking the blood of other creatures (such as Fiends and other Devils).
However, there are instances where more powerful Devils regard other Devils as their children.

It is unclear whether or not their blood is properly nourishing to them, but given consistent remarks that they have a terrible or unusual taste, it's likely that Hybrids aren't as nourishing to Devils as humans (despite being mostly human).
It is unclear whether this rapid aging is a property of all Devils, or just the Control Devil in particular, but it indicates that Devils are capable of aging in general.

Most Devils possess human limbs, faces, bones, and other body parts, such as the Snake Devil's mouth being made of interlocking human arms, even though their fears wouldn't indicate organs or limbs, given the Tomato Devil and Grape Devil both possess human eyes and limbs despite being based on plants.
Other Devils, such as the Fox Devil or the Octopus Devil, don't appear to have these features (at least on what parts of them have been shown).
So far, only two near-death states have been shown: Pochita, the dog-like weakened form of the Chainsaw Devil and the Fire Devil's weakened small-flame form.
Some Devils also have a "near-death" state where their appearance changes to a weaker form.
The 2nd incarnation of the Control Devil first appeared as a little girl, but in the year since the end of Part 1 she has grown significantly, appearing as either a tween or a young teenager.
The ages of most Devils are unknown.
The appearance and physiology of a Devil varies from one to another, as their shape and bodily structure often have to do with the "name" they embody.
There have still been some non-humanoid Devils who have been friendly towards humans, such as the Fox Devil.
This further solidifies because of Aging Devil's existence.
This was first seen when Yoru referred to the Gun Devil and Tank Devil as her "children", given how guns and tanks are weapons typically associated with warfare.(Chapter 176)
Whether Yoru regards them as her children due to their connection with war or the Devils were directly created or birthed from Yoru is unclear.

While fear makes Devils more powerful, consuming blood allows them to quickly heal their injuries as well as grow in power — meaning that consuming humans is more than just instinctual hatred, but often necessary to their survival.
Yoru also implies that there are strict social hierarchies among Devils, stating that bullying is common due to a lack of social fluidity when she comments on Asa's classmates bullying her.
According to statistics, 7 out of every 20 Japanese citizens are killed by Devils.(Chapter 101)
Devil Hunters will sometimes capture Devils to use them for contracts, such as the Future Devil.

Due to the danger that Devils represent to society, many buildings (including schools) have alarms especially designed to warn people in case the building is currently being under attack by a Devil, similar to a fire alarm.(Chapter 107)
For that reason, some Devils and Fiends are coerced into helping humans out of fear of dying rather than doing it out of their own free will.
However, if someone is attacked by a Devil and survives, the insurance won't be as large as it is if such person dies.(Chapter 217)
However, it is worth noting that Devils do not have human rights and, therefore, there are no legal repercussions if they are killed by a human.
In some rare cases, it might even develop into a romantic relationship.
It can be assumed that these statistics are somewhat similar in other countries, meaning that Devil's attacks are the leading cause of deaths around the globe.
Naturally, most Devils have an innate hatred towards humanity and are extremely hostile considering their requirements to feed on the blood and fear of humans.
Notably, Public Safety Special Division 6 is composed entirely of Devils, except for its leader.
Other Devils outright choose to become Devil Hunters, allowing them to live in human society and buy food with the money that they make.
Some Devils, such as the Fox Devil, choose to form contracts with humans, allowing humans to borrow some of their power in exchange for a sacrifice.(Chapter 11)
Some, however, are relatively friendly and feed by alternative means.

The average Devil usually has a bounty of around 300,000 yen and their bodies can also be sold at the black market, with even weak Devils, such as the Tomato Devil, being worth 400,000 yen.(Chapter 1)

The government created a special insurance for the relatives of a person who is killed by a Devil, being large enough to help improve their quality of life, Asa Mikata's mother mentioned that the funding received would be enough to allow her to attend high school.
While uncommon, it is possible for a human and a Devil, or a Fiend to form an emotional bond.

A Devil, who is one of the more notable examples of this, is the first horseman, whose name is "Shihai" in Japanese, which is meant to be a wordplay on multiple similar but different concepts in one umbrella term in that language, but does not have the same effect in other languages, hence it will get different words as its translation such as Conquest, Control or Domination, to name a few.

As seen with Devil transformations, it is known that there can be full Devils of human origin who exist in the world, but their full scope of having the same basic Devil abilities compared to natural Devils remains unknown.

Devils in Chainsaw Man are essentially a type of thought-form or egregore, which are words used to describe any being, either in real world beliefs or in general fiction, that is born from the thoughts, emotions, concepts or psychology, etc. from one or several people respectively.
Devils specifically being the egregores of human fears towards specific concepts.
Fears can only exist and hold as much strength as they do because of the collective feeling and thinking so.
For example, Primal Fears are represented as the embodiment of fears deep-rooted in the collective unconscious, as that is the most instinctual level in all of humanity.
For example, sharks are a type of fish but the Shark Devil and Fish Devil exist as separate beings, but there cannot be more than one Devil who has those inherit "names" who can simultaneously exist.

Fujimoto has stated in an interview that the reason he made Devils “born out of human fear” specifically was because he is a huge fan of horror movies and thought he could use the opportunity to make a lot of homages and references to the horror genre.
Hellenism holds a belief in many Gods, and that includes those of the underworld.

In a broader relation, Devils and their power system as a whole are beings born from a concept in psychology known as the collective conscious and subconscious/unconscious, which relates to the different levels of the collective mind and things such as feelings, beliefs and instincts of all of humanity.
It also holds a belief in daemons, which are worldly spirits that exist alongside every object in the physical world.
It is unknown if they are highly anthropomorphic Devils or Fiends.
Similarly, Buddhism is a religion that acknowledges a number of deities, though it doesn’t revere most of them as in the cycle of suffering.

The "name" for a Devil would more accurately be the concept(s) for a Devil rather than an actual "name" as the names for concepts will not be the same or mean the same thing in different languages and vice versa.
The Primal Devils' bodies are made from or seem to have been made via an amalgamation of human corpses, with Death being the exception.
The Tibetan Book of The Dead in particular presents a whole host of Wrathful Deities that a person is said to encounter following their death.
Their Japanese species name "Akuma" is also used to refer to Satan in Japanese and other demons and Devil figures in media.

There are some Devils from Public Safety, that are not very well known about, but were also said to be Chainsaw Man followers whose names were Seraphim セラフィム Serafimu the bug-looking one who is winged, Dominion ドミニオン the mammal looking one who has hooves, and Virtue ヴァーチェ Vāche the headless Fiend who bears claws.
These beings are not innately evil, but they are fierce and terrifying in a way not too dissimilar to Devils, as not all of them are innately cruel.

This idea stems from concepts like daemons or wrathful spirits of other religions like Hellenism (the Ancient Greek religion – often derogatorily referred to as Paganism) or some schools of Tibetan Buddhism.
While only one type of Devil can exist for a specific "name" for a concept, Devils of similar or larger or smaller categories of concepts can exist.

With how Devils embody concepts and with how Chainsaw Man, specifically, demonstrates the ability to erase concepts from existence by consuming the associated Devils, suggests that Devils have a more profound connection to the nature of reality, human consciousness and the universe as a whole.
Devil Erasure: The Chainsaw Devil is infamously able to consume other Devils, causing the "name" they represent to vanish from public consciousness while also erasing their physical existence.
His ability is, as far as it's known, the only thing that can cease the reincarnation cycle of Devils.
It’s the only form of “true death” that they can experience.
Positive Emotions: Just like fear can make a Devil stronger, positive emotions can make a Devil weaker.
Some concepts, such as nuclear weapons, may be reinvented if all necessary components and primary materials remain available.
When a large group of humans develops love or admiration towards a Devil, those emotions will start to eat the Devil's strength, making them weaker.(Chapter 89)

The Public Safety Devil Hunters 公安のデビルハンター Kōan no Debiru Hantā, later known as The National Devil Extermination Public Safety Commission, are an organization of government-sanctioned Devil Hunters in Japan who function similarly to a Fire Department or Police Force.
They also use badges for identification.
They usually wear formal clothing, such as ties and suits, while Private Sector Devil Hunters do not have to follow a dress code, since they do not work for the government.
They're sent to dispatch Devils in the event of a threat to the public and are tasked with resolving Devil-related incidents on a smaller scale.
This implies that the Public Safety Devil Hunters also have access to better healthcare than civilians and private Devil Hunters.
Though the threat level of the Devils they pursue can vary, they're generally sent after bigger threats than those working in the Private Sector, according to Himeno.
To compensate the fact that Devil Hunters from the public bureau are sent after more dangerous Devils than private Devil Hunters, the government gives them more paid days off and other benefits.

"Fami" is only used in the English and German translation.
Both Famine and Justice are often represented by scales, which can be connected to how Asa originally speculated that Fami was the Justice Devil.
Every other version, except the Polish one, uses "kiga" like in the original.
Fami embodies the Ypositismosphobia (from Greek υποσιτισμός: "malnutrition"), the fear of hunger or starvation.
Fami's earrings are a reference to the Horseman of Famine's depiction in the Book of Revelation, where he is depicted holding scales for weighing food.
Fami's head is nearly always tilted to her left (like an unbalanced scale).
Fami's name is written entirely in katakana (キガ), showcasing no semantic meanings.
Famine is also sometimes interpreted as the "Lord as a Lawgiver".
However, her name is a play on the number of syllables of the word famine to the amount of mora the Hepburn romanization "kiga" has.
In Japanese, the word "kiga" has the same homophone as the Japanese word for "penguin".
Interestingly, the German translation points out that Fami is an English word and in it Fami is the devil of hunger rather than famine.
Like with Santa Claus, Fujimoto likely gave Fami numerous facial moles because he finds that the more moles a character has, the better they look.
So, in the Japanese language, there was meant to be a double comedic effect of how Denji wanted to see penguins and Kiga appears shortly after.

Fami takes on the appearance of a young woman with long unkempt blonde hair that falls in uneven layers and strands.

Like the rest of her sisters, the Famine Devil possesses green multiple-ringed eyes and wears the standard Fourth East High School uniform, similar to other Horsemen Devils attending the high school.
Some of her strands stick out, with bangs across her forehead and sides that reach her ears, and a pair of longer bangs that loosely reach her collarbones.
Fami's name is written in katakana (キガ), though it seems to have no special meaning to it.
However, her name is a play on the number of syllables of the word famine to the amount of mora the Hepburn romanization "Kiga" has.

Although she does not display the same bravado as Devils like Makima and Yoru and can be argued to be benevolent, Fami is still deeply fatalistic, as seen in her way of "saving" humanity: in order to mend her injuries, she spares no thought to an innocent student who wanted to help her and immediately steals his life force.
At the same time, she appears to have somewhat of a high opinion of herself, refusing to take out the trash because it would be a waste of her superior talents.
Despite this, her pleading for Death to kill herself does display that she, in her own warped sense, ultimately sides with humanity over Devils.
Despite this, when she's chastised by a student for her behavior and told to go "crush ants", she actually goes outside to do so.
Fami appears to have a high degree of confidence in her combat skills, and, contrary to her usual personality, is relatively calm and collected in an encounter against a formidable foe.
Fami appears to pity humanity and arrives claiming to save them with her special powers.
Fami has a meek and taciturn demeanor and is very outwardly emotional, in stark contrast with her sisters.
Her notion of salvation seems to be releasing humans from their suffering through death, as she believes her means of doing so will ease any pain that War or Death could cause.
In addition, she does seem to be able to stand up against her sisters as she's able to fire back rebuttals against Yoru when she calls her a weakling.

It can be inferred from her genuine shock at being bested that she may have been a much more powerful fighter at a previous point but had been dramatically weakened to the state she was in at the time of her appearance.

She utilizes basic hand-to-hand combat in attempts to battle the physically imposing Fake Chainsaw Man, analyzes his fighting style, and boldly claims to be capable of defeating him in mere seconds despite being rapidly dismembered by him a moment prior.
She was nervous when introducing herself to students of Fourth East High School, crying throughout her entire introduction and openly bawling when she saw that nobody was paying attention to her.

When she's easily dispatched by the Fake Chainsaw Man, she immediately resorts to begging for her life by offering him a meager ¥2,000 from her wallet, demonstrating an overt cowardice that her sisters lack.
Despite this, she is not above trying to get Death to end her own life to prevent the further suffering of humanity.
Fami has a somewhat more peaceful relationship towards the Death Devil than her other living sibling, likely due to both of them placing value in humanity's existence.
Unfortunately, due to Death managing to turn her into one of her pawns she's now temporarily enthralled by her elder sister and now obediently follows her command.(Chapter 199)
In the present, Fami wanted Chainsaw Man to eat and kill Yoru in order to save humanity, coming to his aid by supplying blood and revving his starter to heal his wounds.(Chapter 218)

"Fami" is only used in the English and German translations.
Every other version, except the Polish one, uses "Kiga" like in the original.
Fami derives her power from Ypositismosphobia (from Greek υποσιτισμός: "malnutrition"), the fear of hunger or starvation.

Fami has supernatural and religious elements tied to her character, most notably her wanting to save people from suffering via death, as the concept of starvation reduces human need to its most basic, undeniable, human level — survival.
Fami's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: Fami ranked 26th in the Third Popularity Poll with 3,441 votes.
In Japanese, the word "Kiga" has the same homophone as the Japanese word for "penguin".
Interestingly, the German translation points out that Fami is an English word and in it Fami is the Devil of hunger rather than famine.
So, in the Japanese language, there was meant to be a double comedic effect of how Denji wanted to see penguins and the Death Devil (under the alias of Kiga) appears shortly after.

This extreme need for mere existence can be paralleled with the absolute, all-consuming nature of faith or ultimate concerns like life and death, reflecting a warped, fatalistic benevolence tied to basic human survival.

Barem's words, however, imply that the price of the contract is one's humanity, with the contractors effectively being transformed into devils.(Chapter 146)

When passed off as the Justice Devil, the Fire Devil, unlike the other Devils, did not seem to ask for any price in exchange for their contract; Yuko tells Asa that the price for her contract is only to receive "a heart that shines with justice".(Chapter 108)

According to Barem, the forms taken by the contractors were initially more hideous and monstrous, but they later adapted and became more similar to Chainsaw Man's as the Fire Devil became more powerful through contracts.
