After returning from Hell and witnessing the power of the Darkness Devil, Power develops severe PTSD, being completely afraid of being alone and feeling that she will be swallowed by the Darkness Devil.
As a result, she needs Aki and Denji to help take care of her, helping her to eat, bathe, and sleep, revealing a more vulnerable side.(Chapter 71)

Contrary to her core values, Power developed such extreme loyalty to her friend Denji that she denied her impulse to sacrifice him to Makima in order to save herself, ultimately saving his life at the cost of her own, and proving that she is capable of putting others before herself.
Power also begins to care for a select few close friends, such as Denji, as evidenced by getting him a birthday cake, and later putting herself in direct danger in order to protect him.
Power also enjoys the thrill of a fight and enjoys showing off her strength and proving her own superiority.
Power has a tendency of imagining several ways of making humans kneel and suffer.

Power is a compulsive habitual liar; after getting in trouble with Makima for killing a Devil when she wasn't supposed to, Power immediately blamed Denji and claimed he told her to kill it.(Chapter 5)
Power is also rude, unkempt, and feels as though those around her should clean up after her.

Power is an insatiable glutton, eating all of the stored food that the team needed in order to survive the Eternity Devil's trap and hoarding food for herself at the Division 4's newbie welcoming party.(Chapter 17)(Chapter 20)
Power is childish, greedy, and almost entirely self-motivated.

Power is once again alive as a result, with her retaining most of her previous timeline's personality such as being bratty and a compulsive liar and quite boisterous and not being someone to abide by authority.
Power sees no difference between pork, beef and human meat; being willing to eat all of them, even if the meat is disgusting zombie flesh.(Chapter 36)
She also appears to care about Aki and is saddened and afraid when he becomes the Gun Fiend.

She also blamed Denji for eating all of the emergency food that the team collected even while she had crumbs on her face,(Chapter 17) and when accused of abandoning a fight because she was scared, Power falsely stated that she ran away merely because she was hungry.(Chapter 29)
She also doesn't seem to fear Nayuta as her superior or the fact that she is the control devil like she was with Makima.
She also shares a loving relationship with her cat, Meowy and is jealous when she sees her cat loving Nayuta more than herself.

She doesn't seem to be a murderous back stabber like before and genuinely helps Denji by offering him blood in exchange for keeping him alive and being his "master" by making him her pet while also keeping the similar sibling like relationship as they had in the previous timeline.
She feels the need to boast her superiority over her fellow Devil Hunters due to her status as a Fiend.
She frequently deflects the consequences of her actions to those around her.
She has no loyalty to humans or Devils, openly admitting that she will join whichever is the winning side.(Chapter 29)
She has no problem gossiping and talking about her friends behind their backs; sharing the secret of Aki's shortened lifespan with the Angel Devil.(Chapter 45)
She hates vegetables, throwing them away when she finds them in her meal.(Chapter 11)
She is highly egotistical and often claims she is capable of doing things she cannot actually do, only to abandon them halfway through when the situation turns sour for her.
She self-admittedly rarely bathes or flushes the toilet and sees humans as being overly sensitive for caring about their hygiene so much.(Chapter 11)
She tends to fight as if she has something to gain and is certain of her victory, and has no problems with running away from a fight where she is outmatched.(Chapter 24)
This compassion prompted her to act for the sake of another being when her pet Meowy was kidnapped.(Chapter 9)
This may be because blood itself is seen as unhygienic, as other fiends aren't explicitly shown being unhygienic.

Though she is extremely selfish, Power was able to experience compassion for the first time towards her pet, after only caring about the smell and taste of blood and the feeling of death when she was killing something.
When asked by Aki about what reward she could want as part of their mission, Power stated that she desired to suck a human's blood until they die.
When promised Denji's blood, Power became ecstatic at the prospect.(Chapter 56)
When she was in front of an swarm of zombies, she got excited and told Denji to watch carefully how she single-handedly defeats all of them.(Chapter 36)

When they were trapped in a hotel due to the ability of the Eternity Devil she spent most of the time there "planning" to win a Nobel Prize and become Japan's Prime Minister so she could raise up their taxes up to 100%.(Chapter 16)
Aki frequently winds up being annoyed by Power's rude and brash tendencies, and she seems to enjoy needling him.
Despite this, she does grow to care for Aki as time goes on, and seems saddened after the events with the Gun Fiend.
Power takes up residence at Aki's home after she joins Public Safety.
The two might be described as developing a similar relationship to a disgruntled elder brother and bratty little sister, with Power constantly causing trouble that Aki has to deal with.
As is mentioned by Makima, Power became a sister figure to Denji, and the two often bicker like siblings.
However, after Denji saves Power and Meowy, they begin living together at Aki Hayakawa's home and develop a more amicable relationship.
In a new world where Pochita never existed, Power ends up saving Denji from the Zombie Collector and makes him form a contract with her.
Like in the old reality, the two become buddies and work together to fight hostile Devils as Public Safety Devil Hunters despite Power's occasional bickering and demands from time to time.
Power and Denji initially had a rocky relationship, with Power being entirely willing to trick and sacrifice Denji to the Bat Devil for Meowy's sake.
Power considers Denji to be her very first friend, and so values him highly.
Power eventually develops strong affection for Denji, even going so far as to deny Makima's wishes and put her own life on the line to keep him safe.
They often bicker and become annoyed with one another, as well as cause trouble for Aki as a pair.
But due to Makima's cold-hearted personality, Makima kills her without remorse.
Even with Power's personality, Makima's unsettlingly calm commands cut through Power easily.
Makima offers Power a chance to be her "pet" again if she hands over Chainsaw Man, immediately turning the worry in Power's eyes to excitement.
Power has always had a deep fear of Makima, likely due to her prowess as the Control Devil.
Despite initially wanting to eat her and taking care of her only so that she could be fattened up, Power cares deeply for her cat, Meowy.(Chapter 7)
She was willing to sacrifice Denji's life to save her from the Bat Devil.(Chapter 7)
When she thought Meowy was dead after being eaten by the Bat Devil, Power became despondent and empathized with Denji before allowing herself to be eaten.(Chapter 7)
Another term for the Powers classification of angels are Authorities.
Dominion and Virtue are also followers of Chainsaw Man along with, Angel Devil, Beam, Galgali, Princi and Seraphim.
Her name originates from Powers, an angel from the middle order of Christian angelic hierarchy along with Dominions and Virtues.
In an interview for Jump Festa 2021, Fujimoto stated that Power's personality was inspired by Walter Sobchak from The Big Lebowski.

In another interview, conducted in Early 2020 for the French magazine ATOM, Fujimoto also states that Power's characterization was based on Eric Cartman, from the American TV animated sitcom South Park, who is similarly foulmouthed and rude.

On one of Tatsuki Fujimoto's alternate Twitter accounts, he has dumped some concept art and what seems to be an early design for Power which may have served as inspiration for Akane Sawatari as she has light-colored hair (as both still have now), with snake eyes and seen with a snake or serpent-like creature wrapping around her.

Power derives her power from blood phobia, also known as hemophobia or hematophobia, an extreme irrational fear of blood, but mostly due to the scary and disturbing connotations surrounding the gruesome sightings of blood spill and the fear of bleeding/blood loss.
Power fits within the body-related devils alongside the Ear Devil, the Legs Devil, the Muscle Devil, the Mouth Devil, the Skin Devil and the Teeth Devil.

After Fire Punch serialization ended, Tatsuki published a new oneshot in Jump SQ 2018-06 Issue, titled Sisters.
After Tatsuki was able to recover his main Twitter account, the temporary one he created was made inactive.
After graduating, he made several one shots participating in Manga Awards Contents and had won some of them and got noticed by ONE and Sui Ishida.

During November 2022, Tatsuki lost access to his primary account nagayama_koharu and created a new temporary one under the user handle @ashitaka_eva, at first fans were skeptical of his identity until Fujimoto's editor Shihei Lin confirmed his identity to fans through this tweet and Tatsuki shared some prototype designs for Aki, Power, and Denji's hybrid form on his new account.
Fujimoto won Honorable Mentions in the November 2013 Shueisha Crown Newcomers' Awards for his debut one-shot story "Love is Blind".
He is active on Twitter as @nagayama_koharu, where he tweets in character as an imaginary younger sister in third grade.
He made his official debut in Jump SQ.19 with "Shikaku" and following year published "Nayuta of the Prophecy" in Jump SQ.
In December 2018, he started a new serialization Chainsaw Man in Weekly Shonen Jump.
In Junior High School he thought of a magazine in his head and often cut and serialized new works in it, usually serializing seven works.
In his first years of high school, he started to upload manga to the website Shintosha.
Later those oneshots were republished on Jump+ or Jump SQ.19 magazine.
Tatsuki made his first serialization with Fire Punch in 2016, ran for eight volumes, published on Jump+ site.
Tatsuki often drew images at an early age.
The series ran for 8 volumes and gathered the internet attention due to its shocking developments.
The series was proposed for a Jump SQ magazine, but as it was declined, the editor proposed it for a Jump+ serialization and it was approved.

The man wishes to know why devils are so interested in getting the Chainsaw Devil’s heart.

When driven into a corner by the Falling Devil and having the chance to turn Denji into a weapon against Asa's wishes, Yoru ultimately had a change of heart and stopped herself, admitting she could not bring herself to do so.

While initially greeting her cordially, Yoru does not hold her sister Famine in high regard, as she insults Famine for interfering with her battle with Chainsaw Man by attempting to heal him and derides her as a weakling.(Chapter 218)
Although it eluded her for a while, Pochita is her fabled arch-nemesis Chainsaw Man, who she hopes to defeat in order to regain Nuclear Weapons and get revenge.
Furthermore, due to their prior encounter, the fear of war became so minute that she was afraid that she'd fade out of existence.(Chapter 104)

Her desire to defeat the Chainsaw Devil, however, has unfortunately consumed her; even though she acknowledges that transforming the Gun Devil and Tank Devil — two Devils that she considers to be her own children — into weapons would completely invalidate her goals of freeing her comrades, she does so just so she can have the chance of defeating her nemesis and prove that she is better.(Chapter 176)
She despises him for defeating and weakening her which caused wars to cease and in turn reduced her to a shadow of her former self.
She hates him to the point where she had a meltdown after she's unintentionally saved by him from the Bat Devil.
To her dismay the situation repeats itself as they are saved by him once more during the Falling Devil fight, after which Asa falls in love with Chainsaw Man, much to Yoru's protests.

Although ambiguous at first, Yoru's scars are visible to other characters, as noted by Yoshida and Miri Sugo, who specifically mentions her scars and Yuko recognizes immediately that it's Yoru she's talking to when seeing her scars.
Although her being able to make contracts could disrupt the notion of Yoru and Asa being explicitly a Fiend, or they could be part Devil and a Human, as Yoru didn't possess Asa fully.
As Yoru and Asa share a body, they could quite literally be called a "war hawk".
Coincidentally, the symbol for Athena, the Greek goddess of warfare, was an owl.
Furthermore, Asa's surname, Mitaka 三鷹, contains the character for "hawk/falcon" (鷹) (taka).
In politics, a war hawk or hawk is someone who favors war.
In some regions of South America, spotting a potoo is believed to be a sign that someone's death is approaching.
In the English version, it specifies Yoru sacrificed 400,000 out of 3.5 million members instead of 40,000, which was stated in the Japanese version, which is most likely a mistranslation.
Owls are birds of prey, which often symbolize war or warriors.
Taylor: "War has always been the mother of invention".
The Gun Devil and the Tank Devil, who Yoru considers her children, could be a reference to the quote by the historian A.
The Nightjar is associated with a short story written by Kenji Miyazawa “The Nighthawk Star”.
The story relays the Nightjar experiencing existential guilt over its actions of killing insects in order to survive, a near identical plight and memory Yoru attained from the same bird.

Yoru and Asa's exact species or "type" hasn’t been confirmed or explicitly stated in the manga as of currently, which has led to much debate about their species, but for simplicity of the wiki and until otherwise is confirmed, Yoru will be referred to as a Fiend with Asa as her living host.
Yoru is also the only Devil seen possessing two bodies as a Fiend and the only case of Devils possessing animals.
Yoru's initial stolen bird form is that of a Nightjar bird that closely resembles an owl or potoo.
Yoru's predilection for making swords or edged weapons may be a reference to the depiction of the Horseman of War in the Book of Revelation, where he is depicted holding a sword.
Yoru's rankings in the Popularity Polls are as follows: Yoru ranked 16th in the Third Popularity Poll with 10,463 votes.
Anemia/Low Blood Amount: Yoru will suffer from anemia when she was fatally injured, which causes her to lose strength if she cannot replenish her blood supply.
To counteract this, Yoru must consume a copious amount of blood to refill her strength.(Chapter 229)(Chapter 230)
